local readiness separate from remote connectivity; omit connectivity state when no supported
observer exists. Shutdown MUST cancel active children and finish resource cleanup before stopping
owners. Reset, cancellation, and shutdown states take precedence over late completion/error events.
Actor stopping alone is not a substitute for domain cleanup. Review teardown ordering in framework
hooks, not just ordinary cancel-button transitions. Follow `.specify/memory/xstate.md` for practical
design and review guidance.
- App: SvelteKit 3, Svelte 5, TypeScript, Jazz (`jazz-tools` v2).
- UI: semantic HTML controls, native Svelte CSS, CSS variables; no Tailwind.
- Complex UI flow: XState with `@xstate/svelte`.
- Localization: Paraglide JS; English is the initial locale, and no visible strings are hardcoded in components.
- Installable shell: native SvelteKit service worker and a web app manifest. Cache public page shells and assets only; keep Jazz data/auth/sync out of runtime caching. Workbox is deferred.
- Native wrappers are deferred.
- GitHub organization/URL namespace: `https://github.com/delightful-labs/`.
- Spec Kit artifacts in `.specify/` and `specs/` are the project source of truth; the inherited plan file is a migration reference/scratchpad.
- Before implementation, keep requirements, technical plan, and task checklist aligned. Resolve consequential ambiguity in the spec before building dependent features.

- Every application feature and production code path needs appropriate unit and Playwright end-to-end coverage. Do not run tests until the user has reviewed and approved the exact implementation being tested.
- Use Prettier for formatting. Keep formatting configuration in the repository and do not reformat unrelated files.

- Work incrementally: complete one focused task per review cycle, using a small related set of files (typically 4–6 implementation files). Multiple routes/components may change together when the task requires it. Discuss larger batches before proceeding; do not spread a change across dozens of files without explicit authorization. Present the change and wait for review before starting another task.
- Do not add timestamps such as `createdOn`/`updatedOn` where Jazz system audit fields already provide them.

This constitution governs implementation and supersedes conflicting project conventions. Amend it when a deliberate architectural decision changes, and update dependent specs/plans in the same change. Each feature plan must state how it complies with the principles above.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Jazz schema and permission design memory
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text: Read this before designing Jazz data relationships, permissions, or persistence behavior.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Local usability is independent of remote freshness
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
Verified against the published `jazz-tools@2.0.0-alpha.59` package and official docs during
[startup research](../../specs/013-local-first-startup/research.md). Recheck source on SDK upgrades.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Local usability is independent of remote freshness
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
- Ordinary browser reads default to local data with upstream propagation. `ReadTier.LocalFirst`
  explicitly includes cached records and pending local writes while synchronization continues.
  `LocalFirstUnlessEmpty` can wait for a remote first answer when empty; `Remote` waits offline.
  Neither belongs on a path that must immediately use already available local data.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Local usability is independent of remote freshness
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
- Ordinary mutation/mergeable-transaction completion should wait for `local` persistence, with later
  rejection observation retained. `global` means server acceptance. Exclusive transaction `wait()`
  confirms authority acceptance and cannot provide offline completion with a remote authority.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Local usability is independent of remote freshness
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
- Server permission enforcement does not require an authoritative preflight for every ordinary
  action. Use current locally known membership/grants and required records; invalidate on observed
  changes. Offline knowledge is not proof of fresh remote permission or erasure after revocation.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Local usability is independent of remote freshness
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
- Separate availability from completeness: an empty local result does not establish global absence,
  first use, or permission to recreate/repair records. Keep initialization provenance, repair,
  seeding, and uncertain-write reconciliation from blocking unrelated locally usable finance work.
  Do not remove idempotency safeguards or blindly replace remote reads in recovery/repair workflows.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Local usability is independent of remote freshness
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
- Persistent browser Jazz already uses a SharedWorker with IndexedDB; memory-driver and external
  runtime defaults differ. Moving application logic into a worker requires explicit verification of
  local-first reads, supported database access, message boundaries, and lifecycle ownership.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Local usability is independent of remote freshness
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
- A service worker cannot construct SharedWorker (Window-only API). Cache public shell/runtime
  assets; do not assume a supported early Jazz handoff, always-running session, or HTTP caching of
  Jazz sync/auth/data. Runtime asset URLs and version identity require a production-build audit.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Local usability is independent of remote freshness
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
The linked draft and backlog distinguish desired changes from current implementation and unverified
optimizations. Preserve separately approved online-only sharing/permission administration and explicit
bank-provider operations; those exceptions must not spread into ordinary local finance workflows.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Local usability is independent of remote freshness
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
Consolidated spec 013 verification adds these boundaries (see
[`investigation-results.md`](../../specs/013-local-first-startup/investigation-results.md)):

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Local usability is independent of remote freshness
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
- An online snapshot is not proof of cold query coverage. A never-opened shared-workspace probe
  returned permitted rows online but encountered `NotObserved` after browser restart, including
  with explicit LocalFirst and authorization-fact warming. Verify exact cold query shapes; do not
  treat coverage failure as remote absence or proof of physical byte erasure. Later controlled
  two-identity probes on the same SDK retain 5,000 permitted of 10,000 records across cold restart
  with an unanswered connection, including root/scoped/ID queries. Metadata-only roots also retain
  permitted references without bytes; a later explicit online request fetches content. The earlier
  failure remains unexplained. See cold-query-follow-up.json; neither probe establishes coverage
  for every relationship, permission scope or history.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Local usability is independent of remote freshness
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
- A compiled WebAssembly.Module can be cloned in memory but cannot be stored in IndexedDB under
  the current WebAssembly serialization rules. Chromium, Firefox and WebKit probes rejected it
  with DataCloneError. Do not design a persistent compiled-module cache from older guidance.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Local usability is independent of remote freshness
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
- Attachment links must inherit transaction read access, not merely check parent existence. The
  reverse files-read inheritance composed with that rule fails publication on alpha.59 for the
  current organization/account predicate. The supported alternative uses files' existing direct
  transaction relation: files require transaction read access AND an attachment matching both
  fileId and transactionId. Parts inherit file reads. The full-app permission suite verifies
  owner/admin, all-account member/viewer, selected grants, denied accounts, unrelated users,
  mismatched-organization grants and cross-transaction links. Unlinked files remain unreadable.
  Preserve both the direct read and matching-link checks; publication alone does not prove access
  correctness. See spec 013 reproductions/README.md for the rejected expression and alternative.
  Cold coverage remains unproven; this authorization repair does not enable broad preparation.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Local usability is independent of remote freshness
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
Retained background query choice also needs a projection check. In spec 013's controlled alpha.59
probes, one-shot snapshots stayed stale after the observed one-second remote-edit window. Public
select('id') subscriptions retained updated/new full transaction fields and audit metadata across
cold restart; ID-only file/link queries retained full metadata without file-part acquisition. At
5,000 readable transactions, retained ID queries added 10.3 MiB page heap versus 21 MiB for full/audit
rows. Both public subscriptions still deliver full result arrays per update. These are page-only,
single-sample measurements, not worker/storage budgets or guarantees for every relationship. See
preparation-cost-follow-up.json under spec 013. Prefer testing public ID projection before accepting
full-row global materialization or assuming a private counts-only subscription is necessary.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Reuse proven reference patterns; verify the exact predicate shape
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
The Check implementation is a working precedent for validating a row's single foreign-key
reference. `transactions.checkId` points to a Check, and `checkReferenceCondition` requires the
referenced Check to match the transaction's organization and account. The permission uses a
positive `policy.checks.exists.where(...)` query with values from the transaction row context.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Reuse proven reference patterns; verify the exact predicate shape
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
That precedent does not establish that every cross-row invariant is expressible. In particular, a
single foreign-key existence check is different from comparing two referenced sibling rows to one
another, or from expressing a negative relationship-existence query. Do not infer a Jazz limitation
from a rejected policy until comparing it with the working schema, permission helper, and policy
tests already in this repository. Also do not infer support for a more complex predicate just because
a simpler Check reference works.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Reuse proven reference patterns; verify the exact predicate shape
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
Atomic database writes and permission expressiveness are separate questions. An exclusive
transaction may atomically stage and settle multiple rows while the server policy still rejects the
predicate intended to validate those rows. Diagnose the exact policy expression and runtime error
before changing the data model or proposing a different persistence authority.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Full-policy linked deletion in alpha.59
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
The production transfer schema uses explicit `s.rel` references from a transfer to both endpoint
transactions. A transaction endpoint must remain undeletable while a transfer row references it,
even after its `internalTransferId` marker has been cleared. Keep the marker-clear write separate;
then delete the transfer row and the selected transaction rows together in the final mergeable
bundle. The full app policy suite verifies this bundle at global durability.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Full-policy linked deletion in alpha.59
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
The transfer deletion and insertion permissions must preserve write access to both endpoint
accounts. On alpha.59, two nested `canWriteAccount` predicates prevented the new paired transaction
from settling globally. Use the equivalent factored transfer-specific predicate: owner/admin or
all-account write access, or a selected-account member with write grants to both endpoint accounts.
An earlier experiment applying this to inserts rejected the browser flow; the later investigation
identified the separate circular insertion dependency rather than treating that warning as final.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Full-policy linked deletion in alpha.59
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
[Jazz's documented transaction authorization](https://jazz.tools/docs/auth/permissions) permits
references to the transaction's own independently authorized writes, but not new rows granting each
other access in a cycle. Transfer endpoints requiring the new transfer, and the transfer requiring
both new endpoints, form such a cycle. Rearranging boolean expressions or write order does not fix it.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Full-policy linked deletion in alpha.59
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
The user approved direct account-based insertion authorization for new **manual** transaction rows,
including their forward marker, while retaining all existing reference/access checks and full
transfer endpoint validation. Authorized standalone manual orphan markers are now an application
integrity boundary, not an insertion denial. Provider inserts do not gain that exception. Keep marker
update guards, financial-fact immutability and transfer/read/delete checks; do not replace local
settlement with global waits or split the three-row atomic operation. Verify accepted roles/grants,
forged-fact atomic rollback, provider orphan rejection and manual orphan/update boundaries explicitly.
Linking already-accepted provider endpoints has a separate cycle: both marker updates require the
new transfer, while its insert previously required both new markers. Transfer insertion now accepts
complete matching endpoint facts with either both markers pointing to that transfer or both markers
clear. The latter anchors authorization in accepted unlinked rows and also admits the already-supported
pending-unlink state. Both-account write access and marker-update guards remain mandatory; mismatched
facts and endpoints claimed by another transfer are rejected. New links write all six side-specific
account/amount/currency facts. Synced-provider browser fixtures must confirm global acceptance before
linking; link fixtures also confirm global acceptance so optimistic UI cannot conceal rollback.
See `docs/transfer-creation-permission-investigation.md` for the exact decision and reproduction.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Full-policy linked deletion in alpha.59
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
Before relying on a new policy shape, validate it against the installed Jazz version and its actual
policy test/runtime path. Include both accepted and rejected cases for the precise relationship and
correlation being introduced.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Full-policy linked deletion in alpha.59
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
Spec 013's final acquisition investigation supersedes its initial LocalFirst background proposal:
use Remote-tier ID subscriptions only for independent server-facing acquisition, leaving foreground
reads/saves LocalFirst/local. Global LocalFirst views stayed stale after observed grant removal;
Remote subscriptions passed grant/member/admin/profile/link changes in all three browser engines.
Use a real wire proxy for silent-transport tests: page routeWebSocket mocking did not reliably block
the SharedWorker. Real-proxy subscription-only tests retain full fields/audit/inserts/deletes and
on-demand file metadata cold. See remaining-investigation-results.json under spec 013.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Full-policy linked deletion in alpha.59
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
Correct replication does not qualify a startup sweep: 5,006 initial records caused a roughly
three-second main-thread long task. Public retained orderBy(id)/offset/limit pages reduce individual
stalls and retain tested cold coverage/live boundary behavior, but increase acquisition time greatly.
Budgeted paging/growth/scheduling requires a statechart and focused review before production adoption.
Never equate a local callback, a count, or independently timed page results with global completeness.
Namespace deletion retained identity in the disposable test, but does not certify OS eviction or
whole-origin recovery. The Chrome quota override allowed writes over its reported quota, so actual
quota-failure handling remains unverified. No private storage/SDK workaround was used.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Full-policy linked deletion in alpha.59
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
Dedicated-worker preparation was tested on alpha.59 in all three desktop browser engines. Public
createAccountManager with a custom AccountStore, restoreLocalFirst and createDb can open a worker
client and receive authorized live queries. However, both persistent and memory worker settings
left zero records available to a cold page; the matched persistent page control retained all records.
The SDK's window-based runtime detection selects a direct worker client rather than the browser
persistent SharedWorker path. A matching identity/app/env/dbName does not establish shared storage.
Public runtime asset overrides do not supply a replica attachment; inspector ports and static worker
factory methods are internal, not application APIs. A 5,000-row worker sample avoided the page's
roughly 2.7-second stall, but failed the persistent preparation purpose. Do not implement this worker
owner or copy rows back through application writes. See spec 013 worker-preparation-results.json.

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Full-policy linked deletion in alpha.59
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
Spec 014 retention verification adds a transaction-tier boundary on alpha.59:
the completed-history query returned 101 rows at Remote tier outside the browser
transaction but zero at Remote tier inside it. The same machine passed its Node
full-policy test, so that alone did not establish browser behavior. Acquire the
authority snapshot before the exclusive transaction, then recheck at LocalFirst
inside it and require matching attempt and account-result identities before
staging the atomic deletion. Terminal log records are immutable under the policy.
Browser retention and full-policy tests verify this path; unit tests reject
partial/mismatched local knowledge. See
[`spec 014 verification`](../../specs/014-bank-sync-log/verification.md).

3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.section: Alpha.60 transfer predicate semantics
3f78e323ff0fc40d63728944c3c899da4ad90ea6.text:
The minimal transfer-policy fixture now permits clearing both endpoint markers and deleting the
relationship in one mergeable bundle when its explicitly declared final-state predicates hold.
Its transaction-update policy is `always`, and transfer-delete requires both endpoints unlinked.
The prior alpha.59 rejection was an SDK evaluation behavior, rather than an explicit deny in those
rules. The alpha.60 fixture verifies the final deleted relationship and both cleared markers.
Finance's production workflow retains its existing staged unlink sequence; this compatibility
qualification does not relax access checks or the restrictions on deleting referenced endpoints.

ab33b9623c572aa1293acdae8acfce5526f222c4.text:
These are user-approved conventions from the message consolidation review. Read this before adding
or changing messages, labels, noun forms, or their callers. Apply the patterns across the message
catalog; account and transaction are examples, not the limits of the convention.

Never edit Paraglide message catalogs, configuration or generated files without
specific user authorization. A general feature or UI request does not authorize
translation edits. Before proposing new strings, give the user a list containing
each exact string, its purpose and location in the code, and why an existing
string or generic action/label cannot serve that purpose. Wait for explicit
approval before adding them. Reuse existing strings whenever possible. Apply
this rule before any other instruction here to consolidate, rename or remove
messages. An explicit request to remove a particular message authorizes that
removal only. Do not regenerate Paraglide files without authorization to do so.

Treat a successful local save as saved. Say “Saved”, without “locally”, remote
acceptance caveats, replication explanations or notices about locally available
history. Users do not need those implementation details. A dedicated Jazz sync
status design is deferred until the user chooses to add it. Preserve technical
persistence/settlement distinctions internally for correctness without narrating
them in ordinary UI feedback. Keep UI copy and assistant communication concise;
do not add explanatory notices the user did not request.

Store regularly used entity nouns under `nouns`, with Paraglide plural variants selected by `count`.
Use the shared noun in standalone labels and as an interpolated argument. Do not keep separate
`labels.account` and `labels.accounts` copies alongside `nouns.account`.

Move reusable verbs into `actions` and reusable label structures into `labels`. Replace the old
entity-specific messages and migrate their callers. Adding more entity-specific strings does not
satisfy a request to consolidate strings.
Concrete examples:

| Before                                           | Shared message                                   | Caller input                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| `accounts.filters.legend`: `Filter accounts`     | `actions.filter_subject`: `Filter {subject}`     | `subject: m['nouns.account']({ count: 2 })`  |
| `accounts.filters.all`: `All accounts`           | `labels.all_subjects`: `All {subjects}`          | `subjects: m['nouns.account']({ count: 2 })` |
| `accounts.manage`: `Manage accounts`             | `actions.manage_subject`: `Manage {subject}`     | plural account noun                          |
| `bank.discover`: `Discover accounts`             | `actions.discover_subject`: `Discover {subject}` | plural account noun                          |
| `labels.account_name`, `labels.workspace_name`   | `labels.subject_name`: `{subject} name`          | singular account or workspace noun           |
| `labels.account_type`, `labels.transaction_type` | `labels.subject_type`: `{subject} type`          | singular account or transaction noun         |

For a standalone collection heading, the count selects the plural noun without displaying a number.
For an actual quantity, pass the real count. Noun messages own grammatical number; do not append
English suffixes or branch on `count === 1` in components.

Message keys containing interpolated text identify their inputs. Use `subject` for an entity noun,
`subjects` for a plural noun, and `name` for an actual user/provider-assigned record name. Use the
same names in the key, message placeholders, and caller arguments.
- Replace `actions.add: Add {name}` with `actions.add_subject: Add {subject}`.
- Replace `actions.select: Select {name}` with `actions.select_subject: Select {subject}`.
- Use `labels.all_subjects: All {subjects}` for a plural noun.
- Use `status.saved_subject: {subject} saved.` for a generic save confirmation.

- Use `status.saved_subject_name: {subject} {name} saved.` when the record's actual name is included,
  for example `subject: m['nouns.account']({ count: 1 }), name: account.name`.
- Use `actions.move_up_name: Move {name} up` when moving a particular named record.
- Use `transactions.daily_total_amount: Daily total: {amount}` for an amount-bearing message.

Plural noun keys remain entity names such as `nouns.account`; their `count` input selects a grammatical
variant. Ordinary interpolated messages identify all displayed inputs in their keys.

Presentation translates and composes localized noun/action messages. Machines may carry message
keys/descriptors; keep their references aligned without changing workflow behavior for a wording
cleanup. Do not turn these straightforward message calls into controllers or workflow abstractions.

Keep context-specific validation, recovery, security explanations, and instructions intact when
abstracting them would lose meaning. A shared short phrase is a clear consolidation opportunity;
a longer sentence merely mentioning an account is not automatically the same reusable structure.
Do not replace proper names, actual record names, or persisted default category names with generic
entity nouns.

When reviewing a cleanup, inspect the whole catalog for remaining repeated structures and every
renamed key's callers, including contracts, metadata, and existing test fixtures. Remove obsolete
keys rather than leaving compatibility duplicates. Compile Paraglide, format touched files with the
repository configuration, and check types. Follow the repository's implementation-review gate before
adding or running tests; mechanical updates to existing key references do not add coverage.

Keep strings rendered inside reusable photo components in their own component catalog (for example,
`messages/photo-cropper/{locale}.json` and `messages/image-editor/{locale}.json`). Keep Finance-owned
modal titles, attachment validation, persistence feedback, and other consumer labels in
`messages/{locale}.json` under `images`. Compose shared image format and size guidance from separate messages in each consumer. Component catalogs own their internal controls and accessible labels;
Finance consumers use Finance messages rather than reaching into a component catalog.

b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.text:
These are user-approved working preferences from the CI and browser-test cleanup. Apply them to
both unit tests and end-to-end tests. The constitution and implementation-review requirements
remain authoritative.

b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.section: Inspect and update tests before running them
b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.text:
- Every implementation change needs an explicit assessment of the affected tests. Search for
  direct coverage and callers, shared fixtures, helpers, and assertions that depend on the changed
  behavior. Identify this impact during implementation review, rather than waiting for failures.

b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.section: Inspect and update tests before running them
b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.text:
- Read the relevant implementation and tests together. After implementation approval, update the
  affected tests before executing them. Apply this to unit and Playwright coverage, including
  parameterized cases and other suites that share the changed contract.

b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.section: Inspect and update tests before running them
b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.text:
- Check unit-test inputs, mocks, return values, machine events/states, validation expectations,
  and persistence outcomes against the current implementation.

b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.section: Inspect and update tests before running them
b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.text:
- Check e2e fixtures against current schemas and permissions. Inspect routes and inherited query
  parameters, accessible roles/names, input values versus rendered text, disclosure state,
  workspace-switch behavior, redirects, and local versus remote persistence expectations.

b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.section: Inspect and update tests before running them
b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.text:
- Follow the approved behavior in the spec. Do not weaken assertions or change fixtures merely
  to conceal an application defect. Preserve the scenario's intent and fix production code when
  the implementation is wrong.

b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.section: Inspect and update tests before running them
b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.text:
- Static inspection complements execution. Run the smallest relevant checks after correcting
  the issues visible in code; do not launch a broad suite simply to discover stale expectations.

b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.section: Inspect and update tests before running them
b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.text:
- For local-first startup changes, cover a cold restart with every app client closed and an online
  connection that opens but never answers, as well as browser offline mode. Check available local
  data and writes, partial replicas, observed access changes, and later rejection or recovery.
  A warm tab or browser online status does not prove cold-start availability or remote acceptance.
  Expand verification when shared behavior changed or evidence justifies it.

b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.section: Inspect and update tests before running them
b261a8e8fc23c68e8d596f634d855dc6e87e0c7d.text:
- On failure, inspect the error, page snapshot, fixture, and implementation before the next
  attempt. Avoid blind retries and longer timeouts as substitutes for diagnosis. Track any
  user-specified retry limit per test and stop/report when it is reached.

- When the user's development server is running, run preparation, type checks, unit tests,
  builds and agent browser servers in a separate checkout with its own `node_modules` and generated
  files. A different app port and in-memory Jazz server do not isolate SvelteKit's generated
  development environment modules. Do not symlink the running checkout's `node_modules`: Vite caches
  and framework-generated dependency files must also be isolated. Verification once overwrote the
  running frontend's Jazz URL with a stopped test server and left workspace preparation waiting.

- The protected environment is the user's `pnpm dev` server: app port 5173 and Jazz port 5174.
  Do not stop it, clear its browser storage, or modify/reset its Jazz data for agent tests.

- Keeping an agent server running is allowed and preferred for successive focused test runs.
  Start `pnpm dev:agent --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5182` (or another available agent port), announce
  its URL, and reuse that server. Its Jazz storage must remain disposable and in memory.

- Match Playwright's base URL and server URL to the agent port. For an explicitly started,
  known agent server, use `reuseExistingServer: true` or the equivalent external-server setup.
  Use isolated browser contexts and fixtures; avoid paying server startup and compilation costs
  for every individual test.

- Reuse only servers known to belong to the agent session. If a port is occupied by an unknown
  process, choose another port instead of killing it. Distinct concurrent agent sessions need
  distinct app ports and disposable Jazz services.

- A sandbox denial when binding a local server is an environment/startup failure, not a failing
  test. Use the available permission mechanism for the authorized local-server operation; do not
  repeatedly retry unchanged tests in a sandbox that cannot start their server.

- Missing `node_modules` is not a reason to skip checks or tests. Install the lockfile-pinned dependencies with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then continue with the relevant checks and tests. Report only a concrete installation failure as a blocker.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
These are user-approved architectural lessons from the bank-sync refactor. Read this before
implementing complex workflows, authorization, readiness, or derived UI capabilities. The
constitution is authoritative; use the active feature artifacts for behavior requirements.

The connected Finance graph targets unpatched `xstate@6.0.0-beta.1` and
`@xstate/svelte@6.0.0-beta.0`. Historical v5 examples below describe ownership,
not current authoring syntax. Read the exact installed package's docs and stability
manifest before relying on a beta API.

- Calculations can be repeated. Return immutable context patches; enqueue mutable
  bookkeeping and native effects. Mutating a `WeakSet` while selecting a spawn can
  reject the recalculated transition and lose the child.

- Invocation input is selected before its owning state's entry context patch.
  Bind it from the admitted request or assign binding/generation in the incoming
  transition. Retain the same facts for later settlement and drain correlation.

- A targetless `{}` consumes an event. Broad native lifecycle handlers must reject
  unrelated actors with `undefined`, before enqueueing, so the corresponding invoke
  handler can run. Prefer invoke handlers or explicit payload matches.

- Completed/failed children can be removed before their notification arrives.
  Use completion output, and retain recipients with the leases whose later release
  needs them. A child disappearing is not a resource-release acknowledgement.

- The installed Svelte binding's `useActorRef` still calls `stop()` on destruction.
  Own roots explicitly when graceful shutdown and financial/native cleanup must
  finish first. Public actor refs do not confer ownership of start/stop lifecycle.

See `specs/013-local-first-startup/xstate-v6-finance-implementation.md` for
qualification and the still-pending application-worker handoff.

Apply this gate **before writing the implementation**, not after the user identifies a complex
function. It applies recursively to helpers, promise actors, nested callbacks, transaction bodies,
and code already inside a machine file. Function names such as persist/prepare/commit and comments
such as "one atomic effect" are not evidence that the operation is a leaf.

1. List the operation's independently meaningful steps, decisions, acquired resources, and terminal
   outcomes in the current plan or a short design note. Classify it as a leaf operation or a workflow.
2. Start with an XState machine if it contains any of these:
- Sequential business decisions, including read -> inspect results -> choose whether/what to write.
- Distinct stages that need separate cancellation, error, retry, or outcome handling.
- An acquired resource whose lifetime spans read/check/write, commit/rollback, or cleanup paths.

3. Define states, guards, events, resource ownership, and interruption/cleanup paths first. Then add
   invoked child machines and leaf actors. Do not first implement a procedural async workflow and
   wrap it in `fromPromise`, or plan to convert it into states later.

4. A promise actor may execute one leaf operation: query a related snapshot, generate IDs, stage an
   already-decided set of inserts, request commit, await settlement, or request rollback. Related
   `Promise.all` reads and an unconditional insertion loop can remain one leaf. Combining these
   stages into a promise that makes intervening business decisions is orchestration and fails the gate.

5. Before presenting the change, inspect each changed actor **and the functions/callbacks it calls**.
   Verify that every workflow step is visible as a state/invocation and every business branch as a
   guarded transition. If not, refactor before claiming the change is ready for review. Report the
   state sequence and any retained boundary invariant briefly; type-checking does not validate this gate.

Preserve one SDK transaction across child-machine states when its API supports that lifetime:
open -> read -> guarded checks -> stage writes -> commit -> settle, with rollback/cleanup on the
appropriate paths. Inspect the SDK rather than assuming callback or cancellation semantics.
Do not split the writes into separately committed transactions just to expose more states.
If the SDK requires a callback with restricted lifetime, document the actual restriction and model
policy and resource ownership explicitly; do not invent unsupported async transaction boundaries.

A narrow transaction-time invariant recheck may remain imperative when necessary for atomicity,
but it must repeat an already-modeled decision, not introduce the workflow's only policy check.
It does not justify hiding acquisition, queries, policy decisions, writes, commit, and cleanup in one
promise actor. Pure validation/transformation, type narrowing, and low-level resource-boundary
handling are not workflows merely because they contain conditionals.

Rejected: async persist function -> promise actor wrapping that function -> parent machine invoking
a commit promise that still reads, checks, writes, and commits internally. Each revision leaves the
nested workflow hidden until that nested operation becomes its own resource-owning machine.

Required: persistence owner validates/hydrates and invokes a transaction child. The child owns one
transaction, guarded eligibility, staging, commit, settlement, and rollback; its leaf actors contain
no new orchestration. Apply the same reasoning to the next nested helper without waiting for another
user correction. Do not turn every expression into a state or create one machine per trivial SDK call.

Write down the states, observed facts, events, ownership tree, and terminal outcomes before effects.
Include cancellation, identity/workspace changes, retries, and shutdown in that first model. For
larger work, show the statechart to the user before implementation.

Sequential business `if` statements are a signal that a child machine may be missing. State derived
from two or more conditions usually belongs in XState. Apply this review inside actors and helper
files as well as components. Moving a function into a machine directory or wrapping it in
`fromPromise` does not expose its decisions to the statechart.

For example, preparation that checks identity, permissions, ownership, and existing/new connection
selection should be a machine with guarded transitions. Its database queries and UUID generation
are focused actors. The same applies to transaction acceptance/omission, mapping eligibility, and
complete/partial result classification.

Do not mechanically turn every predicate into another actor. Guards express decisions, context
stores data, pure functions transform values, and simple form/disclosure state stays local. Keep
low-level abort/disposal checks in resource adapters. Atomic transactions must recheck invariants
inside the transaction, even when a machine already checked them before the write.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Compose small actors with clear owners
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
Put machine definitions in `src/lib/machines/`. Integration components bind subscriptions and
platform dependencies, own or attach actors, forward observations, and compose pure presentation.
Do not replace a large component script with a large controller file.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Compose small actors with clear owners
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
Use child machines for independently understandable workflows: initialization, authorization,
preparation, setup, mapping, account traversal, and individual transaction processing. Invoke children
whose lifetime follows a state; spawn dynamic children under an explicit parent and stop obsolete
ones. Avoid manually starting child actors and awaiting them through promise bridges.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Compose small actors with clear owners
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
Application readiness starts before SDK initialization. It owns startup and the workspace/integration
subtree once dependencies become available. Keep identity, workspace, membership, and credential
readiness distinct. Model supported observations only: browser online status is not proof of Jazz
sync connectivity, and a missing SDK observer is a reason to omit that state.
Model available local data and locally known authorization independently from initialization
provenance, optional seeding, attribution repair, reconciliation, and remote freshness. A known
local membership and grant may permit an ordinary action without a remote response; an empty or
partial replica cannot authorize bootstrap, restoration, or repair. A recovered identity must not
be treated as new because its local query is empty. Identity, workspace, membership, or grant
replacement invalidates scoped decisions immediately; later observations can restore them.
Local persistence is an observed outcome distinct from remote acceptance, rejection, or an
unknown remote outcome. Preserve operation identity and recovery facts across interruption;
do not replay an unknown write or block unrelated local work while seeking remote resolution.

Status-to-message mappings belong with the owning machine, including connection
status, historical outcomes, import settlement and failure reasons. Publish typed
message descriptors through state metadata or the machine's public view selector;
do not make consuming components interpret domain values using local lookup maps
or conditional chains. Persisted history uses the same machine-owned presentation
contract. Components translate the supplied descriptors with Paraglide and render
them, keeping locale changes reactive. Keep translated strings out of persisted
data and machine context; the machine owns which message applies, while the
component owns translation. Do not add or edit Paraglide messages without the
explicit approval required by localization.md.

- A complex form is one UI workflow with a parent machine owning the form lifecycle, editable/locked
  capabilities, validation readiness, submission, and child operation coordination. Do not split
  unrelated pieces into component-local state and infer an overall workflow in Svelte effects.

- The integration component owns subscriptions and dependency binding, translates Jazz observations
  into typed parent events, creates/attaches the root actor, and coordinates graceful shutdown.
  Presentation receives a discriminated view model derived from the parent snapshot and emits typed
  user-intent callbacks. It does not reimplement multi-fact eligibility or keep duplicate pending,
  permission, or linked-state flags.

- Parent and child boundaries follow responsibility, data ownership, and lifetime. Invoke a fixed
  child when its lifetime follows a parent state; spawn only dynamic populations or lifetimes that
  genuinely do not fit invocation. The parent coordinates through typed events and finite invoke
  outputs or explicit long-lived reports; it does not inspect private child state to reconstruct
  policy. Parallel regions are independent dimensions inside one machine, not substitute actors.

- Actor input is initialization, not a reactive binding. Later observation changes use typed events
  with scope/generation correlation. Avoid Svelte effects that read reactive observation state and
  synchronously write back into that same dependency cycle; render selected actor state through
  subscriptions/selectors.

- Convenience lifecycle hooks must preserve the designed drain protocol. In installed
  `@xstate/svelte@5`, `useActorRef` starts the actor and calls `stop()` on component destruction;
  use it only when immediate stop is the intended lifecycle. A root with graceful child cleanup needs
  explicit ownership and shutdown handling.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Design orchestration boundaries before adding machines
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
A collection of machines is not yet a well-designed actor system. Before implementation, draw the
ownership tree and record each actor's responsibility, lifetime, accepted commands, public reports,
terminal output and cleanup obligations. Review both the statechart and communication protocol.
The current workspace-focused reference is
[`008-actor-orchestration`](../../specs/008-actor-orchestration/spec.md); its deferred tasks are not
permission to refactor unrelated subsystems.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Design orchestration boundaries before adding machines
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
- Choose boundaries by responsibility, independent lifetime and resource ownership, not file size or
  the existence of an async function. Use nested states for phases of one responsibility. A child
  machine is justified when it encapsulates a coherent workflow/resource or independently meaningful
  lifetime. Do not mechanically add one wrapper per step or merge resource owners just to reduce files.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Design orchestration boundaries before adding machines
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
- Prefer invocation for fixed children. Invoke on a compound parent state when the child must survive
  transitions between its normal-work and graceful-drain substates. Use spawning for dynamic
  populations or lifetimes that genuinely do not fit state ownership; crossing sibling substates alone
  does not require spawning. Parallel regions share one machine/context and receive the same events;
  separate actors have their own state and explicit message contracts.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Design orchestration boundaries before adding machines
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
- Treat child context and state paths as private implementation details. Publish small domain reports
  for ongoing readiness/access changes and use invocation output for finite results. Presentation can
  observe public snapshots/selectors; parents should not copy full snapshots and inspect private
  operation fields to reconstruct child policy. Snapshot observation itself is supported and can be
  appropriate at an explicitly designed boundary.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Design orchestration boundaries before adding machines
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
- Actor input initializes that actor; later facts arrive through typed events. Prefer typed recipient
  references supplied through input/events and `sendTo` for ongoing communication. Use `invoke.onDone`
  and `invoke.onError` at finite-operation boundaries. Do not replace local typed relationships with
  a global bus, registry or generic supervisor without a demonstrated requirement.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Design orchestration boundaries before adding machines
Design orchestration boundaries before adding machines
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
- Correlate asynchronous reports with their dependency binding and operation/observation generation.
  Invalidate published capabilities immediately on identity, environment, scope or authority changes.
  Equal workspace IDs do not make an old result current after switching away and back. Store observed
  facts/results in context, not a second lifecycle made of synchronized flags.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Design orchestration boundaries before adding machines
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
- Keep integration components responsible for Jazz subscriptions, dependency attachment and browser
  effects. They must not become the message router that interprets one actor's private state for
  another. Independent UI actors may remain component-owned; actors sharing domain policy/lifetime
  need an explicit coordinating relationship.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Design orchestration boundaries before adding machines
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
- A parent supervises direct children; each resource owner handles its own cleanup and descendants.
  Graceful shutdown is a domain protocol, distinct from actor stopping. Await real settlement where
  required, but never await an acknowledgement from an already failed/completed child. Distinguish
  normal failure output from an actor crash. Preserve shutdown intent against late reports/retries.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Design orchestration boundaries before adding machines
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
- Review the installed XState version and platform adapter semantics before relying on examples.
  Optional inspection should expose actor lifetimes and event causality without logging secrets or
  private finance payloads. Static checks alone cannot validate an ownership or race model.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Design orchestration boundaries before adding machines
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
Before presenting a refactor, explain which boundaries changed, which policy now has a single owner,
and how stale reports, replacement and shutdown are handled. Work one subsystem/review cycle at a
time; leave unrelated audits as explicit unchecked tasks rather than expanding the current change.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Prefer guarded invoke completion over route-only states
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
XState has `entry` and `exit` actions, not a separate `before` hook. Use an `always` transition when
the state represents a meaningful assessment or decision. Avoid adding a transient `before...`
state solely to check interruption and immediately route to the next invoked operation. Put those
guards and routes in the preceding invoke's ordered `onDone` transition array instead. This keeps
the completion boundary and its next decision together without adding a state that has no behavior
of its own.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Prefer guarded invoke completion over route-only states
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
Keep a separate state when it owns a real business decision, needs to be observed while work is
pending, accepts its own events, or performs a distinct operation. Do not remove assessment states
such as `assessingCheck` just because they use `always`; their guarded branches are the workflow's
policy. Likewise, `entry` actions are synchronous and do not replace an invoked operation or its
error path.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Prefer guarded invoke completion over route-only states
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
Guards select a transition from the current context and event before that transition's actions run.
If an `onDone` route depends on the invoked result, inspect `event.output` in the guard. If it depends
on a value being assigned by the same transition, either derive the decision from `event.output` or
keep a distinct decision state after the assignment; do not expect the guard to see the new context.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Prefer guarded invoke completion over route-only states
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
When an invoke acquires a resource, every completion route must retain that resource in context
before entering cleanup. If interruption arrived while acquisition was pending, route to rollback
with the acquired handle assigned. After staging, check interruption in `onDone` and roll back
instead of starting commit. This replaces a route-only gate without weakening cleanup or allowing a
late result to start more work.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Prefer guarded invoke completion over route-only states
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
Represent complete success, partial success, cancellation, and failures as actual states. Return typed
terminal results so parents route outcomes without interpreting error-message strings. Classify an
outcome once; persistence receives the chosen outcome rather than recalculating it from counters.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Prefer guarded invoke completion over route-only states
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
Keep observations, counters, scoped data, current resource payloads, actor references, and result
descriptors in context. Do not keep a second lifecycle in `phase`, `stage`, `message`, or independent
flags that must stay synchronized with the statechart. Discriminants identifying actual data variants
are appropriate; distinguish those from copied lifecycle labels.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Prefer guarded invoke completion over route-only states
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
Readiness, permission, credential completeness, eligible mapping destinations, and available actions
are part of the model. Presentation must not reconstruct these from combinations of props. Render
explicit model choices or tags; translate descriptors and format dates in presentation so locale
changes remain reactive. State metadata can hold message/step descriptors.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Prefer guarded invoke completion over route-only states

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
For XState v5 timeouts, use built-in `after` transitions and a named delay in
`setup({ delays })`. Reuse an existing failure/cancellation transition or target.
Timers automatically cancel when their state exits. A timeout should normally
require only a few lines; do not add manual timers, promise races, helper actors,
extra states or result variants solely to implement it. Add separate states only
when they represent a distinct domain outcome or resource-cleanup obligation.
Stopping an invoked actor discards late results; it does not automatically undo
an external operation. Preserve financial-write cleanup and avoid retries of
uncertain writes. See https://stately.ai/docs/delayed-transitions.

A normal cancel path is not enough. Account for navigation, component destruction, SDK session
replacement, scope/permission changes, credential replacement, reset, and unexpected child errors.

Do not assume `actor.stop()` runs machine exit actions or clears context. Send explicit shutdown,
let active children reach cleanup/terminal states, and only then stop/release their owners. Inspect
framework hook registration order: automatic actor stopping can run before a later cancellation hook.
Protect resetting/shutting-down states from later events that would downgrade their intended result.

Replace transient resource payloads as work advances; clear setup tokens, plaintext credentials,
sealing functions, and provider responses on terminal cleanup. Keep persisted encrypted data separate.
A cancelled effect's late result must not advance the workflow or start another provider request.
Treat already-issued database writes according to the SDK's actual cancellation semantics.

When identities or integrations are replaced, tie detach/completion notifications to the actor they
belong to. Do not let an old component tear down a newly attached workspace. Preserve progress counts
across child boundaries without losing or counting them twice.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Put error handling at the right actor boundary
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
Use `invoke.onError` for failures of invoked actors, including synchronous acquisition/startup
failures and rejected promise actors. Do not catch and rethrow inside each `fromPromise` merely to
assign a workflow-specific error code. Let the owning transition classify the failure once, preserve
required sanitized diagnostics, and enter the appropriate failure/cleanup state. Keep secrets and raw
provider payloads out of persisted results and logs when moving classification.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Put error handling at the right actor boundary
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
Audit every invocation, including long-lived callback observers and machine children, for an
unexpected-error path. An ordinary error state in a child or an `onSnapshot` observer does not handle
the child actor itself failing. Do not send a cleanup command to an actor that has already failed and
then wait forever for its acknowledgement; distinguish failure before resource acquisition from
failure after acquisition. Recovery must preserve cancellation/shutdown priority.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Put error handling at the right actor boundary
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
Errors thrown by actions fail their machine; async actions are not awaited. Do not move fallible I/O
into an entry action and expect a local `onError` transition to catch it. Model independently
understandable operations as invoked actors and their decisions as guarded transitions. Moving a
large async helper into `fromPromise` without exposing its lifecycle is not this improvement.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Put error handling at the right actor boundary
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
Native browser event callbacks run outside XState's processing stack. `invoke.onError` does not
automatically intercept later DOM callbacks or promise rejections started inside `fromCallback`.
Those adapters must bridge native failures using typed events or explicit promise rejection. A
callback actor's internal promise rejection handler can therefore be necessary. Do not mechanically
remove catches or replace them with a generic helper solely to hide the syntax.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Put error handling at the right actor boundary
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
Retain narrow platform/resource handling where cleanup requires it: errors after acquisition must
abort/release resources and await actual settlement. Do not assume a callback actor's disposer runs
on every thrown actor failure; inspect the installed implementation when relying on cleanup ordering.
`try/finally` that clears credential bytes, closes images, or releases timers is resource ownership,
not duplicated workflow state.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Put error handling at the right actor boundary
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
For IndexedDB, keep the compare-and-write synchronous inside the active transaction. Validate policy
in the owning machine, then compare the complete observed value atomically at the write boundary to
protect against concurrent changes. Explicitly own opening, transaction selection, abort settlement
and connection closing as states/children. An abort racing a finished transaction can throw; retain
the narrow native-boundary handler and report the actual commit/abort result. Stopping a promise
actor discards its result and is not proof that its side effect was cancelled.

aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.section: Put error handling at the right actor boundary
aba18d3b296cae5f09a06bbfefb97f03a3ab40d5.text:
References: [invocation errors](https://stately.ai/docs/invoke),
[callback actors and errors](https://stately.ai/docs/actors),
[promise actors](https://stately.ai/docs/promise-actors),
[IndexedDB transactions](https://www.w3.org/TR/IndexedDB/).

Session observers can fail while subscribing or later while reading an SDK snapshot. Handle
acquisition with `invoke.onError`; bridge later SDK callback failures with a typed event. Exit the
observer, unsubscribe, and ask the workspace to finish bank cleanup before exposing recovery.
Restart an unexpectedly failed startup actor on retry instead of sending commands to a dead actor.
Keep late startup snapshots and errors from interrupting shutdown.

Supervise pure availability/history/mapping children before their errors can kill a bank owner with
active operations. Route those failures through the existing shutdown/cancellation states and await
the resource-owning child. A failed or completed bank child cannot acknowledge a subsequent shutdown;
its workspace must classify the failure or finish an already-requested shutdown immediately.

For dynamically spawned workspace errors, match the reported actor ID to the currently owned
reference. Consume stale notifications without releasing a replacement workspace. A child may already
be done while its parent's `onDone` event is still queued; check liveness when forwarding resource
notifications so a completed child does not receive credential payloads through warning logs.
Fallible integration callbacks such as selecting an organization belong in an invoked actor with an
error transition, rather than an entry action that can fail the entire workspace.

Review the complete actor tree after focused changes, including startup and presentation boundaries.
Look for hidden branching promises, duplicated result classification, flags outside the model, and
teardown paths that bypass cleanup. Prefer a small reviewed change over another broad mechanical
rewrite.

When an actor contract changes, update test doubles to accept its typed initialization/observation
inputs and emit its public reports, including binding/generation correlation. A fake child that only
sets private state tags cannot verify a message protocol. Capture reports with a real actor recipient;
test stale-report rejection and actual settlement rather than merely renaming fixture fields.

Follow the repository review gate: do not add or run tests until the user approves the implementation
being covered. Formatting and type checks do not establish runtime correctness. After approval, test
state transitions and visible behavior, especially cancellation/races, cleanup, authorization changes,
partial progress, and parent/child subscription rendering. Do not record an implementation as proven
merely because it type-checks.

The SvelteKit plugin used by unit tests regenerates the same environment files as the dev server.
Finish unit/Svelte checks before starting a browser run; concurrent regeneration can replace a live
server's Jazz environment and produce misleading startup failures. Use the isolated in-memory Jazz
configuration in `playwright.bank-sync.config.ts` for reproducible bank/readiness browser checks.

The completed [orchestration ownership map](../../specs/008-actor-orchestration/architecture.md)
records the application, bank and independent form roots. Keep diagnostic instrumentation at existing
actor creation boundaries; an inspection requirement does not justify reparenting actors or adding a
registry, bus or generic supervisor. Use XState's built-in inspection API and evaluate Stately
Inspector before adding custom tooling. The custom trace adapter was removed at the user's request.
Inspection integrations must exclude credentials and private finance payloads. See
[`inspection.md`](../../specs/008-actor-orchestration/inspection.md) for the current environment-gated
Stately integration, attached roots and verification limits.

Shared SDK session ownership is distinct from a rendered layout's actor lifetime. Coordinate known
identity-changing SDK calls after workspace drain; retain issued calls until settlement, and reattach
even when a recoverable SDK failure retains the same client. Do not extend that guarantee to external
SDK calls or all formerly mounted route actors without an explicit ownership protocol. Keep navigation
failure separate from successful identity restoration; retrying navigation must not repeat mutation.

Remove forwarding/status protocols only after finding their actual production consumer. Startup
acquisition does not also need unused SDK-status commands, and a parent with no snapshot consumer
does not need syncSnapshot merely to preserve its child's lifetime or render a subscribed integration.

A recovered identity can finish profile initialization before its workspace catalog arrives. A first
empty local catalog is not a final absence result. If unscoped entry automatically opens the chooser
for an empty catalog, preserve that entry's route intent so a later sole workspace can canonicalize
it. Keep the intent only for the same ready identity and original route/automatic chooser; discard it
on explicit selection, unrelated navigation, session loss, or an observed ambiguous catalog. Explicit
chooser visits remain independent of ledger selection. Guard the resolution against catalog loading
and errors. Test arrival both during and after navigation; do not hide the race with longer waits or
force ordinary local navigation to wait for remote freshness.

Finance's generic scoped form/readiness/submission/write/controller lifecycle, profile workflow,
workspace initialization/startup, explicit-creation ownership/journal/recovery and restoration
coordination now come from Delightful Local First. Keep Finance files as typed dependency/policy
adapters. Update generic behavior in the library instead of copying machines back into this app.
Native finance schema transactions, financial resource drains, routing and legacy attribution
repair remain app-owned. See `docs/finance-foundation-extraction.md` for the exact boundary.

08e614c76097e7467ed175cfa032409a109d60d2.text: - Follow `.specify/memory/constitution.md` and the active feature artifacts under `specs/`. Before designing or changing complex state, read `.specify/memory/xstate.md`. Before designing Jazz schemas, permissions, or persistence behavior, read `.specify/memory/jazz.md`.

- Never edit Paraglide catalogs, configuration, or generated files without explicit user authorization. Before proposing new strings, list each exact string, its code purpose/location, and why existing strings or generic actions/labels cannot work; wait for approval. Treat local saves as “Saved” in UI, without local/remote caveats or unsolicited sync notices. See `.specify/memory/localization.md`.

- Before adding or changing localized strings, read `.specify/memory/localization.md`. Consolidate reusable action/label structures, use shared plural nouns, and name variable-bearing keys and inputs consistently (for example, `actions.select_subject: "Select {subject}"`).
- Do not use `switch` statements or `case` clauses; use discriminated-union narrowing, lookup records, or clear conditional expressions.
- Work on one task at a time. Do not start another task until the current change has been shown to the user and reviewed.

- Use a small related set of files per focused review cycle, typically 4–6 implementation files. Multiple routes/components may change together. Discuss larger batches first; do not edit dozens of files without explicit authorization.

- Keep Jazz subscriptions, dependency binding, and actor lifecycle wiring in the page or integration component. Define complex workflows and reusable authorization/readiness decisions as focused XState machines under `src/lib/machines/`, composed through child actors. Those files compose imported pure components rather than declaring native HTML from scratch. Pure presentation components receive data and callbacks through props; simple presentation state, UI-library controls, and localization belong there. Extract shared helpers only for genuinely reused logic, not merely to move a page script into a controller file. Do not create components merely to relocate page templates.

- Before writing an async workflow or `fromPromise` body, apply the mandatory machine-first gate in `.specify/memory/xstate.md`. Multiple independently meaningful steps, read/check/write decisions, or an acquired resource with commit/rollback/cleanup paths MUST start as a statechart, including inside transaction callbacks and existing actors. Implement the machine first; promise actors perform individual leaf operations. Wrapping or relocating an async function does not satisfy this rule. Before presenting the change, inspect every new/changed actor and its helpers recursively for hidden orchestration. Use explicit success, partial, cancellation, and failure states; do not mirror lifecycle state in context flags.

- Keep status-to-message mappings in the owning machine or its public view selector, including persisted history outcomes, settlement and failure reasons. Consuming components translate supplied message descriptors and render them; do not interpret domain statuses with component-local lookup maps.
- Keep components small and reusable. Do not invent visual styling or add decorative UI unless the user approves that direction.
- Name entity validation files to match their schema files (for example, `schema/transactions.ts` and `validation/transactions.ts`). Keep canonical validation and its derived form adapters together.

- Do not add or run tests until the user has reviewed and approved the implementation that those tests will cover. Identify affected unit and Playwright tests during implementation review; after approval, update their fixtures, helpers, and assertions by inspecting the implementation before running them. Follow `.specify/memory/testing.md`; do not use repeated test runs to discover drift that static inspection can reveal. Run only the relevant checks.
- Use the repository Prettier configuration. Do not format unrelated files.
- Whenever starting a development server, tell the user and provide its URL so they can open the same server.

- Use `pnpm dev:agent` for agent browser work (default `http://localhost:5180`); it uses disposable in-memory Jazz storage. Agent servers may stay running and be reused across focused tests; start one server and point subsequent Playwright runs at it instead of restarting it for each test.
