81af3f0b18c007697c618881d799bc281c2e0257.text:
Read before designing or extracting reusable library components.
Adapted on 2026-10-31 from Finance `8ff72f6` (identity/workspace compositions and
XState memory) and DUI `9bc5405` (README.md and public exports).
- DUI owns generic buttons, fields, dialogs, popovers, loading/status feedback, and content primitives.
- This library owns reusable identity/session/workspace behavior and their embeddable compositions.
- Consumers own routes, screens, layout, navigation, domain schemas/rules, and domain workflows.

Integration components bind subscriptions and dependencies, attach/own actors, forward scoped typed
observations, and compose imported views. They may access the documented backend integration layer;
SDK calls remain in its adapters. Pure presentation accepts typed data/view models and callbacks,
not database clients, subscriptions, actor refs, or raw snapshots from which it reconstructs policy.
Keep simple draft/disclosure state local; reusable complex state follows xstate.md.

Do not create a component merely to relocate a page template or move a script into a controller.
Extract a coherent reusable responsibility, and extract shared helpers only for actual reuse.
Keep canonical validation and derived form adapters together; entity validation filenames match
schema filenames. Library validation must not absorb Finance-specific entities or policies.

Use `$props`, typed callback props/native callbacks, and child/named snippets supported by the actual
DUI version. Do not assume old slots, bundled triggers, locale providers, or undocumented props.
Forward appropriate native attributes, events, class/style and accessible descriptions through
wrappers without overriding consumer names or creating duplicate IDs. IDs must be safe for multiple
instances. Inspect the public contract before adding a wrapper or proposing a missing primitive.

DUI Dialog provides native modal behavior and a required caller-owned heading; callers supply triggers
and close controls. Native close/cancel/toggle events must stay synchronized with the interaction
owner. Every dismissal route, including unmount and scope invalidation, requests the same idempotent
cleanup. Native dialog focus behavior does not guarantee focus for internal step changes; the
composition owns meaningful step/error focus and the consumer owns its return target.

Use Popover for lightweight contextual choices and a dialog/embedded view for longer sensitive flows.
Do not force full screens or a router. Support usable keyboard paths and manual alternatives to
optional clipboard/QR features. Closing does not imply mutation rollback or clipboard erasure.

Reuse ButtonContent for icon/loading button content when supported by the pinned DUI artifact.
It renders presentation only; operation readiness and pending state come from the workflow owner.
Reuse StatusMessage/LoadingScreen/LoadingSpinner and FieldFeedback for their documented purposes.
Do not nest live announcements. Field guidance describes fields; operation feedback has one status
owner. Keep an announcement region mounted when updates need announcing rather than assuming initial
render text is announced. Label buttons explicitly; decorative icons/spinners remain hidden from
assistive technology.

All visible text and accessible labels follow localization.md. Views translate descriptors and use
consumer-compatible localized messages. Never show recovery secrets in announcements or diagnostics.
Recovery disclosure does not require a saved-phrase acknowledgement. Keep the Close control at
the bottom; dismissal never records a successful backup. Clear sensitive material on every terminal/scope-change path.

Source patterns are extraction evidence, not proof of complete runtime correctness. Finance's
vendored `0.0.25-details-animation` archive and DUI's `0.0.25` checkout can expose different APIs;
pin and inspect actual exports before adoption. Generic missing behavior belongs in a DUI proposal,
not a duplicate library primitive. SDK/toolchain versions and detailed packaging require planning.
Identify affected actor/view/browser tests at implementation review and add/run them only after
approval. Follow this repository's Oxlint/Oxfmt policy, not copied reference-repo formatting commands.

Shared form/profile compositions accept typed views, callbacks, snippets and caller-translated
labels. Their controllers and policy/resource machines are separate public imports. Finance
retains its schema bindings, existing Paraglide callbacks, diagnostic sink, icons and cropper.
Do not import Finance modules or its locale catalog into the library. See `docs/next-app.md`.

d854109d9a64ac46a03c7e5bc6b620c9aef5d60a.section: I. Jazz-First Delivery with Explicit Backend Boundaries
d854109d9a64ac46a03c7e5bc6b620c9aef5d60a.text:
Jazz is the sole required v1 backend. SDK access MUST remain behind documented integration
boundaries for identity/session, workspaces/access, and typed consumer data operations. Ordinary
workflows and presentation MUST NOT call Jazz directly. Consumer-owned SDK-native schemas and
policies MAY remain in identified integration modules. Future backend replacement MAY require
schema/policy mapping and migration; source-compatible portability is not promised. Independent
plugin distribution, a universal schema language, and second-backend qualification are deferred.
App-required capabilities, permissions, and durability MUST NOT be silently weakened.

New application and library code MUST use strict TypeScript and MUST NOT use `any`, type assertions
(including `as` casts), `switch` statements, or `case` clauses. Use `unknown` with narrowing, generics,
`satisfies`, typed adapters, lookup records, or clear conditionals. Model variants with discriminated
unions and required variant-specific fields rather than loosely related optional fields. Bundled
Spec Kit scripts remain inherited tooling and are outside these application-code restrictions.

XState actors and machines MUST own stateful foundation workflows: startup and shutdown, identity
and session lifecycle, recovery, device linking, workspace transitions, and operation lifecycles.
Cancellation, failure, retry, and cleanup MUST be explicit. Backend integrations MUST permit
backend-native methods and steps without pretending unsupported flows succeeded. Pure helpers and
simple presentation state MAY use ordinary functions and Svelte runes or stores; they do not require
machines. Workflow logic MUST remain separate from rendered presentation.

The foundation MUST own reusable identity and workspace behavior, not Finance or Clipper domain
models or workflows. App-specific permission requirements MUST remain expressible and enforceable
through backend integrations. DUI MUST own generic presentation primitives; the foundation MUST compose them for
identity and workspace interactions. Missing DUI primitives MUST be documented as evidence-based
recommendations with explicit ownership, rather than assumed to exist or implemented implicitly.

Account/recovery, device-linking, and workspace-membership dialogs, popovers, and reusable views MUST
be embeddable across consumer apps. Consumers MUST retain ownership of full screens, routes,
layouts, and domain workflows. Presentation components MUST receive data and callbacks through
props and render independently of backend sessions, queries, and XState actors; integration modules
and composition boundaries MUST connect those concerns. Components MUST NOT be created merely to
relocate templates.

Interactions MUST use semantic controls, support keyboard operation and meaningful focus and
dismissal behavior, and expose accessible operation feedback without duplicate announcements.
User-visible strings MUST be localizable from the beginning through Paraglide; reusable compositions
MUST support consumer localization. Transient sensitive recovery and device-linking information MUST
be cleared when its interaction ends. Detailed library localization integration remains a design
decision, not a requirement for consumers to adopt foundation-owned routing.

d854109d9a64ac46a03c7e5bc6b620c9aef5d60a.section: VI. Explicit Data and Access Guarantees
d854109d9a64ac46a03c7e5bc6b620c9aef5d60a.text:
Private workspace data MUST be protected at the backend/storage boundary, independently of UI
visibility. Shared workspace membership and available access levels MUST follow the selected
backend's documented model; the foundation does not require generic read-only membership. Additional
app-specific restrictions are required only when explicitly approved as consumer product requirements
and then MUST be enforced at the backend/storage boundary. Code patterns observed in a reference app
do not alone establish a product requirement. Qualification MUST document offline availability,
permission-change timing, revocation limits, failure semantics, and relevant capability limits.

d854109d9a64ac46a03c7e5bc6b620c9aef5d60a.section: VI. Explicit Data and Access Guarantees
d854109d9a64ac46a03c7e5bc6b620c9aef5d60a.text:
Operations advertised as locally durable MUST survive an offline restart. Local acceptance,
durability, connectivity, and synchronization MUST NOT be conflated. Consumers MUST observe distinct
startup, loading, empty, ready, and error outcomes. Obsolete subscriptions MUST be released when
consumers, sessions, or workspaces change and MUST NOT expose another identity's data. These rules
constrain implementation of the user-approved shared data boundary and identity behavior recorded
in the active feature specification.

Future production behavior MUST have appropriate automated coverage: unit tests for logic and state
machines, focused backend-boundary checks, and Playwright coverage for user-visible workflows,
authorization, and offline behavior where feasible. Implementation MUST be reviewed and approved by
the user before its implementation tests are added or run. After approval, required checks MUST pass
before the feature is considered complete. Jazz MUST demonstrate the agreed v1 required capabilities; a deterministic fake MAY support routine
tests but MUST NOT replace verification of Jazz persistence and storage authorization.

- Shared UI MUST use Svelte 5 and DUI. Repository-owned app or demonstration hosting MUST use
  SvelteKit; reusable components MUST NOT require consumer adoption of its routes or layouts.

- Localization MUST use Paraglide. UI styling MUST use native CSS and CSS variables, without Tailwind.
  Until a visual direction is approved, repository-owned UI MUST remain unstyled and wireframe-like.
- Stateful workflows MUST use XState, with Svelte integration kept outside pure presentation.

- Use the installed Oxlint and Oxfmt tooling and repository configurations. These replace the prior
  Prettier policy. Preserve tabs, single quotes, no semicolons, no trailing commas, and 100-column
  width where supported; avoid unrelated formatting.

- Repository runtime and package-manager requirements are recorded in `package.json`; the lockfile
  pins installed tooling dependencies. Application toolchain compatibility, package boundaries,
  Svelte lint/type-check coverage, and detailed localization integration MUST be settled through
  design or tooling review before dependent implementation. Installed repository tooling does not
  establish application-stack compatibility or backend qualification.

- Follow the active feature in `.specify/feature.json` and its artifacts under `specs/`. Requirements,
  plans, and tasks MUST remain aligned before implementation of dependent work.

- The current phase remains specification-only. Foundation code, plugins, demonstrations, and
  consumer migrations MUST NOT be implemented without a new instruction authorizing that work.

- Follow the user's resolved Q1 (shared data abstraction) and Q2 (cross-app identity) decisions in
  the active feature specification. Other unanswered consequential decisions MUST remain explicit
  until resolved; dependent contracts MUST NOT treat assumed answers as approved requirements.

- Jazz alone MUST qualify against the agreed MVP capabilities. Additional backend evaluation and
  independent plugin contracts are deferred and MUST NOT gate v1.

- Complete one task at a time and present it for review before starting another. Change no more than
  one route or component per review cycle unless the user authorizes otherwise.

- Do not add or run implementation tests before approval of the implementation they cover. Document
  review and static consistency checks MAY validate specification artifacts in this phase.

- When starting a development server, tell the user and provide its URL. Never commit or publish
  without explicit authorization.

This constitution governs project design and implementation and supersedes conflicting repository
conventions; explicit user instructions take precedence. Every feature plan MUST state compliance
with these principles and identify unresolved decisions before dependent work begins.

Amendments MUST explain their rationale and affected artifacts and be presented for user review.
Approved amendments MUST reconcile affected specifications, plans, and repository guidance through
explicitly scoped review tasks. Deferred reconciliation MUST be recorded rather than silently treated
as complete. The initial tooling follow-up is complete: repository configuration and `AGENTS.md`
now use Oxlint/Oxfmt. Subsequent design proposals remain subject to their own review.

Constitution versions MUST follow semantic versioning: MAJOR for incompatible principle removals or
redefinitions, MINOR for new principles or materially expanded guidance, and PATCH for clarifications
that do not change obligations. Amendments MUST preserve the original ratification date and update
the last-amended date. Compliance reviews MUST check backend boundaries, guarantees, ownership,
accessibility, unresolved decisions, and the applicable review and validation gates.

Version 2.0.0 replaces the mandatory independently distributed multi-backend MVP with Jazz-only
v1 delivery at the user's explicit request. The shared data boundary remains, while portable
schema expression and a second real backend cease to be release requirements. Strict typing,
XState ownership, privacy, accessibility, and implementation review gates remain in force.
The active spec and repository guidance are reconciled in this documentation change. The old
technical plan is marked superseded; detailed design artifacts require reconciliation in the
next reviewed planning task before implementation. This amendment does not authorize code.

4b79eff3eb71f6f280998fd754515aa9cb47337b.text:
Read before styling library compositions or introducing public CSS properties.
Adapted on 2026-10-31 from DUI `9bc5405`, especially README.md, theme.css,
ButtonContent.svelte, Dialog.svelte, and StatusMessage.svelte. DUI observations are
reference conventions, not authorization to redesign its components.

Use native CSS and custom properties; no Tailwind. Reuse DUI presentation and documented tokens.
Library compositions own necessary internal layout; consumers own page layout, responsive placement,
and visual direction. Keep the initial composition wireframe-like until a visual direction is approved.
Prefer scoped layout with grid/flex and gap. Preserve logical DOM order and use logical dimensions
where appropriate. Do not reach into DUI internals using descendant selectors or styling classes.
Use public props, snippets, native class/style forwarding, and documented custom properties.

DUI's theme is optional and global when imported: it changes body/control defaults, colors, typography,
and focus treatment. Its `dui-theme` cascade layer allows application overrides. The library must not
silently import a global reset/theme or force consumer styling. Preserve usable fallbacks without it.
Use documented DUI spacing/color/typography tokens rather than inventing a parallel design system.

DUI registers component properties in their owning component and shared tokens in theme.css.
Registrations are global even when declared in a scoped Svelte style block. Each property has one
registration owner; consuming components must not register it again. Never redefine `--dui-*` tokens
or registrations in this library. New library-owned public properties need a distinct documented
namespace selected during interface design and one registration owner.

For a genuinely new public property, document inheritance, purpose, accepted values, and fallback.
Typed `@property` declarations require computationally independent initial values. Universal syntax
without an initial value can preserve contextual/complex values but provides no narrow validation.
Preserve inheritance for intended ancestor overrides and fallback chains. Do not copy typed defaults
that would mask contextual fallbacks or relative theme values. Registration is an API decision, not
necessary for every local variable.

Retain native focus, dialog/popover behavior, visible labels, viewport bounds, and usable scrolling.
Motion or a spinner cannot be the only indication of state. Follow DUI's decorative icon/spinner
conventions so feedback has a single announcement owner. Do not introduce decorative styling as part
of infrastructure extraction.

After implementation approval, test behavior, native state, accessibility, focus, visibility, bounds,
and scrolling. Do not assert computed/inline CSS or class names and do not select elements by styling
classes. Styles may set up a behavior scenario without becoming the asserted result. No test execution
is authorized by this memory update.

eefe6e4f82f7a3f8f83df67380df8fc655c67271.text:
Read before adding or changing messages, labels, accessible names, or message callers.
Adapted on 2026-10-31 from Finance's `.specify/memory/localization.md` at `8ff72f6`
and DUI's caller-owned label conventions at `9bc5405`.
Share reusable verbs under `actions` and label structures under `labels`. For example:

| Key                         | Message                   | Input                                 |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `actions.select_subject`    | `Select {subject}`        | localized workspace noun              |
| `labels.subject_name`       | `{subject} name`          | singular localized noun               |
| `labels.all_subjects`       | `All {subjects}`          | plural localized noun                 |
| `status.saved_subject_name` | `{subject} {name} saved.` | localized noun and actual record name |

Use `subject` for a noun, `subjects` for a plural noun, and `name` for a user-assigned name.
Variable-bearing keys identify displayed inputs consistently with placeholders and caller arguments.
Plural noun keys remain entity names such as `nouns.workspace`; `count` selects their variant.
Migrate callers and remove obsolete duplicate keys when consolidating a structure.

Keep wording consistent for the same action. Use Select for existing choices; Create is appropriate
for workspace creation. Do not import Finance-specific nouns or entry wording into this library.
Keep recovery/security instructions and context-specific validation intact when abstraction would
lose meaning. Whole sentences remain translatable; never assemble them with English concatenation.
Reusable short templates must still be reviewed for the grammar of supported locales.

The library owns messages for the internal controls, instructions, errors, and accessible labels of
its identity/workspace compositions. Consumers own app navigation, domain text, and app-specific
operation explanations. DUI receives caller-localized strings/snippets and does not acquire a
foundation translation dependency or generic English fallback.

Keep reusable component catalogs separate from consumer catalogs. Consumers must not reach into
private component catalogs for their own labels; shared public labels require an explicit supported
contract. Do not import Finance's generated Paraglide module or catalogs into this library.

Presentation translates and formats; machines emit typed outcomes or message descriptors rather
than retaining translated strings. Changing locale must update visible and accessible text without
restarting operations. Do not build a controller merely to relocate ordinary message calls.

Before implementing catalogs, the technical plan must settle library message packaging, generation,
consumer overrides, locale propagation/SSR isolation, and supported locales. These conventions do not
select a process-global locale singleton or impose foundation routes/middleware on consumers.

Inspect all renamed callers, including contracts, metadata, and existing fixtures. Compile Paraglide,
check types, and format touched files with this repository's tooling once that integration exists.
Follow implementation review approval before adding or running tests. This documentation task adds
no catalog, generated output, dependency, or build integration.

933e5b397d02ab3a3cb640a5412a8cab8f5e8031.text:
Read before designing stateful workflows, readiness, authorization, or async operations.
Adapted on 2026-10-31 from Finance's `.specify/memory/xstate.md` at `8ff72f6`.
The constitution and active spec define scope; these rules do not authorize implementation.

The library now targets the exact v6 beta in `package.json`. Use schemas, function
transitions, immutable context patches, `createAsyncLogic` for async leaves and
`createCallbackLogic` for native event adapters. Queue selected effects with `enq`.
Prefer direct actor sources; use `createInvoke` to retain generic input/output
inference. The form writer retains a registered source name for its union of a
native leaf and consumer-supplied persistence logic; it remains a v6 source.

Final states support entry/exit actions and output. They do not handle transitions
or start invokes/timers. Keep terminal context patches and queued cleanup on their
owning final entries; preserve resource drain before completion.
Do not depend on a completed child remaining in `children`. Handle native failures
from their reported events, and use the transition's scoped child references for
ongoing work. Pure named predicates remain useful; compose them with ordinary JS
instead of v5 guard combinators. Review parallel-region reentry explicitly. A total, effect-free routing node uses
`type: 'choice'`; a conditional wait or a context/effect-producing eventless step
uses `always`. Classify each event by sender before using `internalEvents`: child
and native callback reports are not self-originated events.

Use the published XState package without patches or declaration overrides. Group
related generic lifecycle values in explicit immutable context records and update
the complete record when any member changes. This keeps ownership visible and
lets v6 check source/target context compatibility. Where a generic union output
cannot be expressed through the beta's schema inference, use an explicitly typed
output mapper and let the machine infer that output contract. See
`specs/003-verified-backup/xstate-v6-implementation.md`. Historical v5 API references
below describe the original ownership rules, not supported imports.

Read `node_modules/xstate/docs/index.md`, `agents.md` and `api-stability.json` for
the exact installed beta before migration reviews. Apply the evidence and
per-repository requirements in `specs/003-verified-backup/xstate-v6-design-review.md`.
Source inspection, type checking and runtime qualification are separate gates.

Before writing an async function or `createAsyncLogic` body, list meaningful steps, decisions,
resources, and terminal outcomes in a design note. Start with a statechart when there are
read/check/write decisions, independently meaningful stages, distinct retry/cancellation paths,
or an acquired resource spanning commit/rollback/cleanup. Apply this recursively to helpers,
transaction callbacks, and existing actors. Wrapping procedural orchestration in a promise actor
or moving it to a machine directory does not satisfy the gate.

Define states, guards, events, ownership, interruption, and cleanup first. Promise actors perform
individual leaf operations. Pure transformation, narrowing, and narrow resource-boundary handling
may remain imperative. Do not mechanically create one state or actor per expression or SDK call.

A transaction owner must model eligibility, acquisition, staging, commit, settlement, and rollback
where those are real steps. Keep one atomic transaction when required; do not split writes merely
to expose states or invent async boundaries the SDK cannot support. Recheck atomic invariants at
the write boundary after the modeled decision. Inspect actor helpers recursively before review.

- Keep reusable machines under `src/lib/machines/`. Choose children by responsibility, resource
  ownership, and lifetime rather than file size. Draw the ownership tree and public protocol first.

- Invoke fixed children whose lifetime follows a state. Spawn dynamic populations only when their
  lifetime warrants it. Avoid manually starting children and awaiting promise bridges.

- Use typed events/reports for continuing observations and invocation output for finite results.
  Actor input initializes; subsequent facts arrive through events. Child context/state paths remain
  private. Do not introduce a global registry, bus, or supervisor without a demonstrated need.

- Use `enq.sendTo` in the state that owns the recipient invocation.
  Do not rediscover a fixed child's lifetime through `self.getSnapshot().children` for routing.
  Nested handlers must include the parent's interruption/binding actions explicitly. Send only
  commands the child can receive; promise leaves settle under the owner's drain protocol. In
  parallel regions, keep existing control-state precedence when the work state sends commands.

- Give each readiness/access decision one owner. Context holds observed facts, payloads, references,
  and results; states own lifecycle. Do not duplicate lifecycle in phase fields or pending flags.

- Correlate reports by dependency binding and generation, not just workspace ID. A → B → A must
  reject old A reports. Invalidate scoped decisions immediately on observed identity/access changes.

- Integration components own subscriptions, dependency binding, actor attachment, and browser effects.
  SDK adapters provide backend leaf operations; machines consume typed boundaries. Presentation
  receives selected view models and callbacks, not SDK handles or actor policy to reconstruct.

Keep local availability, initialization provenance, remote freshness, persistence, and authority
acceptance distinct. Locally usable work must not wait for optional seeding, repair, or reconciliation.
An empty replica is not evidence of a new identity or permission to recreate data. Unknown writes
retain identity/recovery facts and are not blindly replayed.

A complex form has one workflow owner for editing/submission, validation readiness, capabilities,
and operation coordination. Simple disclosure, draft input, and UI-library state may remain local.
Do not infer domain readiness from combinations of component flags or reconstruct access in views.
Translate message descriptors and format values at the presentation boundary so locale changes react.

Use explicit success, partial success, cancellation, and failure states with typed terminal results.
Classify outcomes once. Guards run before transition actions; inspect `event.output` when routing
on an invoke result rather than expecting a same-transition assignment to be visible to the guard.
Use meaningful decision states; avoid transient routing-only states where invoke completion guards
already express the decision.

Every invocation needs an unexpected-error path, including observers and child machines. Entry
and exit actions are synchronous; async actions are not awaited. Invoke fallible I/O. DOM and SDK
callbacks outside the actor stack must bridge errors with typed reports or an explicit rejection.
Do not remove narrow resource cleanup catches merely to hide syntax.

Cancellation, unmount, identity/workspace replacement, access loss, retries, and child crashes must
respect resource ownership. Retain an acquired handle even if cancellation arrived during acquisition,
then clean it up. Stopping a promise actor discards output; it does not prove side-effect cancellation.
Closing a dialog does not undo a committed write or identity transition.

Graceful shutdown is a protocol: request drain, settle active work, clear secrets, then stop owners.
Do not assume `actor.stop()` executes exit actions or clears context. Never wait for an acknowledgement
from a failed/completed child. Check framework hooks against the installed adapter: automatic stopping
may run before later cleanup hooks. SDK session ownership may outlive a rendered layout; drain scoped
work before identity-changing calls and track issued calls until settlement. Retry navigation separately
from a successful identity mutation.

Before implementation review, inspect the whole changed actor tree for hidden orchestration, stale
reports, secret retention, duplicated classification, and cleanup bypasses. Identify affected unit
and browser tests; add or run them only after implementation approval. Static checks do not prove races
or cleanup. Inspect at existing actor boundaries without changing ownership or logging private data.

Forms, workspace initialization/startup, durable explicit-creation ownership/recovery, profile
editing and restoration coordination expose typed factories under documented public subpaths.
Consumers inject policy/schema/storage capabilities rather than fork these statecharts.
Caller-supplied promise capabilities still must be leaf operations; the factory boundary is not
an exemption from recursive workflow review. Host application lifetime owns a Jazz startup
registry, and layout attachments do not acquire competing sessions. See `docs/next-app.md`.

f1f8ed65c204244535ab24b63ac74e378f3279f0.text: - Follow the active feature in `.specify/feature.json` and its artifacts under `specs/`. Follow `.specify/memory/constitution.md` if one is adopted.

- Before designing workflows or async actors, read `.specify/memory/xstate.md`. Before changing localized text, read `.specify/memory/localization.md`. Before styling or composing components, read `.specify/memory/css.md` and `.specify/memory/components.md`. These adapt shared lessons from Finance and DUI; domain-specific reference behavior is not an implicit library requirement.

- Machine changes use the pinned, unpatched XState v6 beta. Adapt library logic to its published APIs and types; do not patch XState. Follow the migration notes in `specs/003-verified-backup/xstate-v6-implementation.md`; retain generic contracts and the existing implementation-test review gate. Read the installed XState agent guide/stability manifest and apply `specs/003-verified-backup/xstate-v6-design-review.md` before treating a conversion as complete.

- The current monorepo task authorizes source relocation and workspace wiring. It does not authorize new foundation behavior, backend plugins, demonstration apps, or consumer SDK migrations. The former specification-only phase remains recorded in history.
- Follow the Jazz-first MVP decisions in the active spec. Earlier Q1/Q2 decisions are resolved; the 2026-10-31 scope revision defers portable schemas and multi-backend qualification.

- Jazz is the only required v1 backend. Keep SDK access behind documented integration boundaries for later replacement; independent plugins and a second backend are deferred. Do not silently weaken app-required capabilities, permissions, or durability.
- Keep Finance and Clipper domain behavior outside the shared foundation. DUI owns generic presentation; this foundation owns identity/workspace compositions.
- Work on one task at a time and present it for review before beginning another. Change no more than one route or component per review cycle unless the user authorizes otherwise.
- Use functions, closures and plain data for application code. Do not introduce application-owned classes or inheritance; stateful lifecycles belong to XState machines.
- Do not use `switch` statements or `case` clauses in new application code; prefer narrowing, lookup records, or clear conditionals. Bundled Spec Kit scripts are inherited tooling.
- Do not add or run implementation tests before the user reviews and approves the implementation they cover.
- Use the repository Oxlint and Oxfmt configurations and avoid unrelated formatting.
- When starting a development server, tell the user and provide its URL.
- Never commit or publish without explicit authorization.

- For v6 machine testing, follow the generated-testing section in `specs/003-verified-backup/xstate-v6-design-review.md`: prefer `@xstate/test` campaigns with independent behavioral oracles; preserve integration tests and existing implementation-review gates.

9ea15f469a4775b5cef7fc053093c545aeffa57a.text: - Use the pinned XState v6 dependency and its schema/function model for machine changes. See [the migration specification and implementation notes](docs/xstate-v6-migration.md).

- Review v6 changes against the installed package docs (`docs/agents.md` and `docs/api-stability.json`) and [the design audit](docs/xstate-v6-design-review.md). Use published XState without patches or declaration overrides.
- Keep workflow decisions visible in transitions with descriptive predicates, return immutable context patches, and queue effects with `enq`. Preserve context-update order when composing patches.
- Interaction machines and their DOM resources belong to the mounting UI component; retain explicit subscription and browser-resource cleanup.
- Test user-observable behavior, native HTML state, and accessibility semantics rather than styling implementation details.
- Do not assert computed CSS values, inline style values, or the presence/absence of CSS classes in unit or Playwright tests.
- Avoid selecting elements by component styling classes. Prefer role, label, text, and native attributes; use stable IDs or explicit test attributes only when no semantic locator is suitable.

- Replace style assertions with behavior checks where possible: for example, verify keyboard interaction, focus, visibility, accessible names/descriptions, layout bounds, or scrolling instead of color, spacing, animation, or specific CSS properties.
- Tests may change styles to set up a behavior scenario (such as a longer animation duration), but should not assert the style values themselves.

- For v6 machine testing, follow the generated-testing section in `docs/xstate-v6-design-review.md`: prefer `@xstate/test` campaigns with independent behavioral oracles; preserve integration tests and existing implementation-review gates.

201308b75473d8cce60961e0ffb45ccc21141619.text: A Svelte 5 component library undergoing an API and styling migration. See [breaking changes](docs/svelte-5-breaking-changes.md) for the current migration reference.
Use [Conventional Commits 1.0.0](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) for pull request titles: `<type>[optional scope][!]: <description>`.

Examples: `feat(details): animate opening and closing`, `fix: restore keyboard focus`, and `docs: clarify setup`. Use `!` for a breaking change and explain the change in the PR description. Choose a title that describes the complete change being merged.

The `Conventional PR title` GitHub Actions check validates titles when a PR is opened, edited, reopened, updated with commits, or marked ready for review. The `Conventional PR titles` repository ruleset requires this check before merging into `main`.
Use Node.js 22.17+ on the 22.x line, or Node.js 24+, and pnpm 10.22.0.

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm dev
```

`pnpm build` builds the development app and the library. `pnpm package` generates `dist`, including declarations, and validates package metadata with publint. `pnpm check` runs static Svelte and TypeScript checks. `pnpm lint` checks formatting and ESLint; format only the files you change with `pnpm exec prettier --write <files>`.

Tests require implementation review and approval before they are added or run. After approval, use `pnpm test:unit --run` for SSR/unit checks and `pnpm test` to build current source and run Chromium scenarios against a temporary production preview on port 4174.
Source imports use `#lib` and `#lib/*`, declared in `package.json`. Public package imports remain `delightful-ui` and `delightful-ui/theme.css`.
Import the optional global theme once in your application layout:

```js
import 'delightful-ui/theme.css'
```

The theme supplies green accents (`#94ff47`), system-preference light/dark surfaces, shared spacing, and base typography/media/focus styles. Button hover uses green with dark text. Jost is the default font for body text and headings. Interactive components—including buttons, details summaries, navigation items, pagination, and form controls—use Cascadia Code through `--dui-font-family-interactive`, which defaults to `var(--dui-font-family-mono)`. Component-specific font-family properties still take precedence. Cascadia Code is used for `code`, `pre`, `kbd`, and `samp`. Both variable fonts are bundled and self-hosted, including real italics, with `font-display: swap`; no requests to external font services are made. Jost supports weights 100–900 and Cascadia Code supports 200–700. Override `--dui-font-family`, `--dui-font-family-body`, `--dui-font-family-mono`, or `--dui-font-family-interactive` to customize the stacks. Font licenses are included in `dist/fonts/`. Without this import, components retain their own styling fallbacks.

Existing consumers that need the pre-bundled-font defaults can import
`delightful-ui/theme-classic.css` instead. This compatibility entry preserves the
Source Code Pro/monospace control and heading stack, system/sans-serif body
stack, and existing sizes/colors/spacing. It maps `--dui-font-family-interactive`
to the existing `--dui-font-family` token and does not import bundled fonts.
Import one theme entry per application. The website and Local First's Storybook
use this entry to retain their existing presentation while linking workspace UI.

Component-specific `@property` registrations live in the owning component's `<style>` and load with that component, independently of the optional theme. Shared color, spacing, typography, border, shadow, and pressed-offset registrations live in `theme-properties.css`, shared by both theme entries. Each property has one registration owner, even when other components consume it. For example, Button owns `--dui-button-*`, InputWrapper owns shared field/input properties, and LoadingSpinner owns its spinner properties.

Registrations remain global CSS definitions; component placement does not scope their names. Use unique `--dui-*` names, enable inheritance for ancestor overrides, and preserve existing fallback chains. Properties using universal syntax (`"*"`) without initial values preserve contextual or complex values; those registrations do not validate a narrower type. Typed registrations use computationally independent initial values. Theme declarations still provide relative units, aliases, fluid spacing, and light/dark colors.
Field labels use the shared `--dui-font-size-sm` token (`0.875rem`, with the same fallback without the theme). Override `--dui-field-font-size` to customize label size independently of input text.

Spacing primitives use rem units: `--dui-spacing-xxs` (0.25rem), `--dui-spacing-xs` (0.5rem), and `--dui-spacing-sm` (0.75rem) stay constant across viewport sizes. Larger tokens use `clamp()` to grow smoothly between viewport widths of 20rem and 80rem: `--dui-spacing-md` (1–1.25rem), `--dui-spacing-lg` (1.5–2rem), `--dui-spacing-xl` (2–3rem), and `--dui-spacing-xxl` (3–5rem). Values stay within those bounds outside that viewport range. The existing `--dui-space-xs`, `--dui-space-sm`, `--dui-space-md`, and `--dui-space-lg` tokens alias `--dui-spacing-xs`, `--dui-spacing-md`, `--dui-spacing-lg`, and `--dui-spacing-xl`, respectively. Components retain their own overrides and honor legacy spacing overrides where previously supported. Shared gaps and padding now use the spacing primitives; medium and larger values grow on wider screens. Avatar Input’s square-to-button gap uses `--dui-spacing-xs`, with a 0.5rem fallback without the theme. Override `--dui-avatar-gap` to customize that gap.

The theme follows the system color preference automatically. Set `data-dui-theme="dark"` or `data-dui-theme="light"` on the root `<html>` element to override it; remove the attribute to follow the system again. Override `--dui-*` properties on the root for application-wide theming, or `--dui-button-*` properties to customize Button.

The stylesheet uses the `dui-theme` cascade layer so ordinary application CSS can override its defaults. It is global when imported: it changes body margins, colors, fonts, box sizing, links, focus indicators, and native control fonts/accent colors. It contains no page layout, heading scale, or form-control replacement.

The compact app typography scale uses `--dui-font-size-xs` (0.75rem), `--dui-font-size-sm` (0.875rem), `--dui-font-size-md` (1rem), `--dui-font-size-lg` (1.125rem), `--dui-font-size-xl` (1.25rem), and `--dui-font-size-xxl` (1.5rem). Sizes stay constant across viewport widths and scale with the root font size. Existing small text retains its 0.875rem size.

```svelte
<Heading level="h1">Account settings</Heading>
<Heading level="h2" size="sm">Notifications</Heading>
```

`Heading` renders a native h1–h6, defaults to `level="h2"`, and accepts content through its children snippet. Default visual sizes map h1 → xxl, h2 → xl, h3 → lg, h4 → md, h5 → sm, and h6 → xs. Optional `size` overrides appearance independently of the semantic level; choose `level` for document structure. Native attributes, events, class, and style pass through. Default margins are zero, so layout owns spacing. Heading uses the typography tokens with matching fallbacks when the optional theme is absent. Customize `--dui-heading-font-family`, `--dui-heading-font-size`, `--dui-heading-font-weight` (600), `--dui-heading-line-height` (1.3), and `--dui-heading-color`.

`Heading` and `Text` accept an optional `align` prop: `start`, `center`, `end`, `left`, `right`, or `justify`. Omit it to inherit alignment. Prefer `start` and `end` for direction-aware layouts. Inline `Text` (`as="span"`) follows the containing block’s alignment; this prop does not position the span within its parent. Use paragraph Text or set alignment on the containing block to align a line of text.

```svelte
<Text>Manage your account preferences.</Text>
<Text as="span" size="sm">Last saved a moment ago</Text>
<Text align="center">Centered paragraph</Text>
```

`Text` renders a paragraph by default; `as` accepts `p` or `span`. Its optional `size` accepts `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, or `xxl` and defaults to `md` (1rem). It shares the `--dui-font-size-*` scale with Heading, including fallbacks without the optional theme. Children provide content; native attributes, events, class, and style pass through. Default margins are zero. Font family uses `--dui-font-family-body`; customize `--dui-text-font-family`, `--dui-text-font-size`, `--dui-text-line-height` (1.5), or `--dui-text-color`.

```svelte
<Button>{saveLabel}</Button>
<Button text={cancelLabel} />
```

Labels are caller-provided strings or child snippets. Button no longer accepts locale objects or reads UIProvider; absent content has no generic English fallback. Provide an accessible label for every button. To use an SVG icon, place its path inside `Icon`; icons are decorative by default and hidden from assistive technology. If the SVG itself conveys meaning, provide `label` for an `aria-label`, `title` for a native SVG `<title>`, or `aria-labelledby` referencing visible text. For an icon-only button, label the button with its action and leave the icon decorative.

```svelte
<Button>
	<Icon style="width: 1em; height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.125em;">
		<path d="M5 12h14M13 6l6 6-6 6" />
	</Icon>
	Continue
</Button>
```
Use a 24×24 viewBox unless the source SVG specifies otherwise. The consuming app supplies the SVG paths; `Icon` provides shared SVG defaults and accessibility behavior.

```svelte
<Icon label="Warning">
	<path d="M12 3 2 21h20L12 3Z" />
	<path d="M12 9v4m0 4h.01" />
</Icon>
```

Field labels render exactly as supplied. Native `required` validation remains; supply your own translated visible marker in the label when needed. Shared `--dui-color-error` adapts invalid styling to the explicit light/dark themes.

Error text and borders use dark red on light surfaces and light red on dark surfaces. Destructive buttons pair this red with `--dui-color-on-error` (white in light mode, dark text in dark mode); dark-mode hover uses a lighter red with dark text. Custom error colors or surfaces should preserve at least 4.5:1 text contrast and 3:1 contrast for error borders.

Button defaults to `variant="raised"`. Use `variant="flat"` for square bordered controls with no default shadow or pressed movement. Flat pressed colors can be customized with `--dui-button-color-active` and `--dui-button-background-color-active`.

```svelte
<FloatingActionLink href={resolvedHref} aria-label={addLabel} title={addLabel}>
	<Icon icon={AddIcon} />
</FloatingActionLink>
<FloatingActionButton aria-label={addLabel} onclick={addItem}>
	<Icon icon={AddIcon} />
</FloatingActionButton>
```

Use FloatingActionLink for navigation and FloatingActionButton for actions. Each accepts its native
HTML attributes and child content directly. The button defaults to `type="button"`; native
`disabled`, explicit `type="submit"`, and form attributes retain their normal behavior. Supply an
accessible name for icon-only controls using `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Title is an optional
native attribute, and Icon is decorative by default. Visible child text can also provide a name.

Both components share a private presentation wrapper: a circular control aligned to the inline end
of its bottom-sticky container. Native class/style and callbacks apply to the actual anchor or button.
Consumers own icons, labels, resolved URLs, query parameters, and actions. Link activation and new-tab
behavior stay browser-native; labels for deliberate new-window navigation should describe that behavior.

The wrapper stays within the caller's scrolling/containing layout. The app owns surrounding spacing
and scroll/layout policy. Customize control size with `--dui-floating-action-size` (default `3.5rem`)
and content/icon size with `--dui-floating-action-icon-size` (default `--dui-font-size-xxl`). Colors,
border, shadow, and focus use the existing theme. Neither component owns application workflow state.

```svelte
<SkipLink href="#main-content">{skipLabel}</SkipLink>
<main id="main-content" tabindex="-1">...</main>

<SkipButton aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls={dialogId} onclick={openTools}>
	{toolsLabel}
</SkipButton>
```

These controls stay available to assistive technology and keyboard navigation while visually
hidden. Focusing a control reveals it at the viewport's logical top/start corner; leaving it
hides it again. Place skip controls early in document order so keyboard users encounter them
before repeated navigation. Their fixed position does not reserve space in the page layout.

`SkipLink` requires `href` and preserves native anchor navigation. Supply an existing fragment
target; give non-interactive targets `tabindex="-1"` when they should receive focus.
`SkipButton` defaults to `type="button"` and retains native Enter/Space activation, disabled
state and explicit form attributes. It can open a caller-owned dialog without changing link
semantics. Both accept native attributes/events, class/style and child content on the actual
control. Callers own translated labels, targets, actions, dialog state and focus restoration.

```svelte
<NumberKeypad
	label="Amount keypad"
	decimalLabel="Decimal separator"
	backspaceLabel="Delete last digit"
	nextLabel="Next"
	onkey={handleKey}
/>
```

`handleKey` receives a `NumberKeypadKey`: a digit string (`'0'`–`'9'`), `'decimal'`, `'backspace'`, or `'next'`. Import that type from `delightful-ui` when typing your handler. All keys are native `type="button"` controls; the keypad does not edit a value, submit a form, parse money, navigate, or listen for physical number keys.

Supply translated labels from the application. `decimalSeparator` changes the displayed character (default `.`) while its command remains `'decimal'`. `disabled` disables every key; `nextDisabled` disables Next independently. Native group attributes, class, and style pass through.

The three-column grid fills its container, with a full-width Next button. Keys use flat Buttons and responsive `--dui-number-keypad-key-aspect-ratio` (default `1`). Override it with `3 / 2` for rectangular keys. Other properties are `--dui-number-keypad-gap` (default `0.5rem`), `--dui-number-keypad-key-min-height` (default `64px`), and `--dui-number-keypad-font-size` (default `1.5rem`). Minimum height and content size take precedence when space is tight. The application owns width, screen placement, amount drafts, caret/focus management, and custom/device keyboard selection.
Use a native name and optional default value for form submission without field state:

```svelte
<InputText
	label="Description"
	name="description"
	defaultValue="Groceries"
	required
/>
```
Native attributes and callbacks pass through. `bind:value` is optional. Use `label` for visible text, `id` for an explicit input ID, and a native datalist ID for `list`.

Native numeric constraints and callbacks pass through. Optional `bind:value` yields a number or undefined; FormData still yields strings. Use `min`, `max`, and `step` rather than character-length truncation.

```svelte
<InputCurrency
	label={amountLabel}
	currencyLabel="USD"
	name="amount"
	defaultValue="12.50"
	pattern={amountPattern}
	required
/>
```

Required `label` and `currencyLabel` are caller-owned strings. The currency label appears beside the native text input and is included in its accessible description. Caller-supplied `aria-describedby` IDs are preserved alongside the generated currency description ID, so FieldFeedback works normally. Use a short currency label such as USD, EUR or a translated abbreviation; no currency name or symbol is inferred.

Optional `bind:value`, `value` and `defaultValue` stay strings. Native FormData submits only the amount draft under `name`; the displayed currency label is not a submitted field. Native reset restores the default. `inputmode` defaults to decimal and `autocomplete` to off; native text attributes/events, disabled/read-only state, class and style pass through. `type` is fixed to text. Customize `--dui-input-currency-gap` (default `0.5rem`); input and field typography use the existing tokens.

InputCurrency does not parse, format, round, clamp, validate currencies, insert separators or convert money to floating-point/minor-unit values. Partial drafts and comma decimals remain exactly as entered. The application supplies locale/currency validation through `pattern` and its own validator, determines allowed decimal places and signs, handles integer conversion and owns keypad/device keyboard selection. There is no default money pattern or keypad workflow.

```svelte
<InputDate label="Date" name="date" defaultValue="2026-10-13" />
```

Values stay as date-only strings; the library performs no Date or timezone conversion. Native `min`, `max`, and `step` constraints pass through. `bind:value` is optional, and `defaultValue` supplies initial/reset text.

```svelte
<InputAvatar label="Avatar" name="avatar" removeLabel="Remove" bind:value />
```

A custom square image picker with a plus icon and cropped preview. The visible `label` is associated with the native file input. A persistent button below the square displays `uploadLabel` (default `Upload`) to choose an image and `removeLabel` (default `Remove`) after selection. Supply these props to customize or translate each label. The control keeps the same size in both states. Click the square to choose or replace an image. Supports a bindable `File | null`, native form submission, required validation, disabled state, and form reset. Customize the tile size with `--dui-avatar-size` (default `8rem`). Selecting a file does not upload it to a server.

```svelte
<InputImage label="Image" name="image" removeLabel="Remove image" bind:value />
```

Choose a single local image with a native file picker. Optional `bind:value` holds a `File` or `null` (the default); parent updates also update the native file input. The Browse control uses the flat button styling and shared `--dui-button-*` tokens, without an outer input border. Its native label follows the browser locale. The selected filename wraps onto multiple lines when needed. The selected image has a decorative preview and a removal button that returns focus to the input. Replacing, clearing, or destroying the component releases its preview URL. A failed preview leaves the selected file available for submission.

Supply translated `label` and `removeLabel` strings. Native attributes and callbacks pass through, including `name`, `id`, `required`, `disabled`, `capture`, and accessibility attributes. `accept` defaults to `image/*` and is a picker hint, not file validation. `type` is fixed to file and selection is single-file. Native form reset clears the image; disabled fields are omitted from submission. Read the selected file with `new FormData(form).get('image')`; use multipart encoding for native file uploads. The application owns uploading and validation.

This custom component has no tag-input dependency. Enter or the Add button adds a trimmed tag; empty values and case-insensitive duplicates are rejected. Commas remain part of tag text. Duplicate drafts remain available for correction, and blur does not commit a draft. Optional `suggestions` appear in a native popover filtered by the draft, excluding tags already selected. Clicking a suggestion adds it immediately. Arrow keys select an option, Enter adds it, and Escape dismisses the list; typing again reopens it. Focus stays in the input. The list follows the input on scroll and resize, opens above it when space below is limited, and stays within the viewport. Browsers without the Popover API retain free-text entry and the Add button.

Optional `normalizeTag(tag)` supplies the comparison key used consistently for duplicate detection, suggestion deduplication, selected-suggestion exclusion and draft filtering. It receives trimmed text, including empty or incomplete drafts; use a pure function that accepts any string. The default is lowercase comparison. It never rewrites displayed tags, bound values, form submissions or announcement labels. Applications retain validation and persistence policies; custom Unicode normalization needs no additional DUI dependency.

Optional `bind:value` reads and updates a string array. `defaultValue` defaults to an empty array and supplies initial/reset tags; reset also clears the draft. Caller-supplied arrays are copied when edited. Supply translated `addLabel`, `removeLabel(tag)`, `selectedTagsLabel`, `addedMessage(tag)`, `removedMessage(tag)`, and `duplicateMessage(tag)` text. These labels and message callbacks are required. `id` and `placeholder` are optional.

Committed tags render as a named list. Additions and removals are announced through a polite status region; duplicate feedback is also visible and leaves the draft intact. Editing the draft or resetting clears feedback. After removal, focus moves to the next remove button, then the previous one if the last tag was removed, or to the input when no tags remain.

Optional `instructions` and `errorMessage` render visible text linked to the input. `errorMessage` marks the input invalid by default; an explicit `aria-invalid` takes precedence. `aria-describedby` accepts IDs for application-provided descriptions and is combined with internal help, error, and duplicate-feedback IDs. The application owns validation; no minimum tag count is enforced.

Chips and the entry controls share a wrapping row, with compact borderless remove buttons and 48px minimum heights. Customize `--dui-tag-gap`, `--dui-tag-entry-gap`, `--dui-tag-min-height`, `--dui-tag-color`, `--dui-tag-background-color`, and `--dui-tag-remove-background-color-hover`; input styling uses the shared input tokens.

Inside a form, each committed tag submits a separate field under `name`; read tags with `new FormData(form).getAll('tags')`. Draft text is excluded, and an empty array submits no fields. `disabled` prevents editing and submission; `readonly` prevents editing but submits existing tags. The component contains no nested form.

Required caller-owned `id` links feedback to any native control through `aria-describedby`. Optional `instructions` and `errorMessage` render plain translated text; when both are supplied, both remain visible. Error text uses the shared error color. Empty or omitted messages render no text, and the empty container stays in the DOM but occupies no layout space. Each field needs a unique feedback ID. Combine this ID with other description IDs when needed.

The application owns validation, issue mapping, `aria-invalid`, focus and announcements. FieldFeedback does not add a default live-region role, so it can describe a field without repeating aggregate form feedback. Native div attributes/callbacks, class and style pass through; supply a role explicitly only when the application needs it. Group the control and feedback with CSS grid/flex and `gap`. Customize `--dui-field-feedback-gap` (fallback `--dui-field-gap`, then `0.25rem`), `--dui-field-feedback-color` and `--dui-field-feedback-error-color`; typography uses the existing field tokens. Existing inputs need no new props to use this component.

```svelte
<Select label="Category" name="category" defaultValue="personal">
	<option value="personal">Personal</option>
	<option value="work">Work</option>
</Select>
```

Options and groups use native markup. Native attributes pass through; `bind:value` is optional. Use strings for single-select values/defaults, or string arrays with `multiple`. Styling shares the field/input tokens and keeps native browser appearance.

```svelte
<Textarea label="Notes" name="notes" defaultValue="First line" rows={4} />
```

Native multiline editing, attributes, and callbacks pass through. `bind:value` is optional; `defaultValue` supplies initial/reset text. Styling shares the field/input tokens, with vertical resizing by default through `--dui-textarea-resize`.

```svelte
<Checkbox label="Receive updates" name="updates" value="yes" defaultChecked />
```

The native control submits its value only when checked and enabled. `bind:checked` is optional; `defaultChecked` supplies initial/reset state. The clickable label and native checkbox use green accent and explicit focus styling.

```svelte
<RadioGroup label="View" name="view" defaultValue="week">
	<RadioItem value="day">Day</RadioItem>
	<RadioItem value="week">Week</RadioItem>
	<RadioItem value="month" disabled>Month</RadioItem>
</RadioGroup>
```

Compose square-cornered radio buttons inspired by [Ant Design's radio buttons](https://ant.design/components/radio/) from two public components. `RadioGroup` supplies the native fieldset/legend, shared name, selection, validation, and reset behavior. `RadioItem` renders a labelled native radio with button styling; its children supply text or non-interactive rich content. Place items directly in the group, render them with an each block, or compose them through application components and layout wrappers. Items inherit the nearest group's state through Svelte context and must be rendered within a `RadioGroup`. Use unique string values within each group, and keep interactive controls outside item labels.

The default layout connects items and wraps on narrow screens. The selected item uses the theme accent and an inset underline. For a custom layout, place a grid or flex wrapper inside the group and set `--dui-radio-border-overlap: 0px` on it to give each item its own border. Item `class` and `style` apply to the label wrapper so apps can control placement; other native input attributes and callbacks pass through, including `id`, `aria-label`, and `aria-describedby`.

Group `bind:value` is optional; `defaultValue` supplies the initial selection and the selection restored by form reset. An explicit `value` takes precedence over `defaultValue`. Without either, the group starts unselected; assigning `undefined` clears a bound selection. Native keyboard navigation, focus, validation, and form submission are preserved. `required` uses native radio-group validation. Group `disabled` disables every item; item `disabled` disables just that choice. Only an enabled selection is submitted. Supply group `name` for a stable form-data key; omitted names are generated per instance so groups remain independent. Group `form` associates every item with an external form. Native fieldset attributes, class, style, and events pass through; group and item `onchange` callbacks receive the native input event after selection updates.

Customize `--dui-radio-background-color`, `--dui-radio-color`, `--dui-radio-border-color`, `--dui-radio-selected-background-color`, `--dui-radio-selected-color`, `--dui-radio-focus-color`, `--dui-radio-padding`, `--dui-radio-min-height` (44px), and `--dui-radio-disabled-opacity` (0.5). Typography, label spacing, and border width use shared field/input and theme tokens. `RadioItem` owns the item tokens; `RadioGroup` owns `--dui-radio-border-overlap` (defaults to the shared border width).

Typography resolves size props through a shared typed font-token lookup and uses one scoped base rule per component. Existing `--dui-heading-font-size` / `--dui-text-font-size` overrides and native inline styles remain supported; omitted alignment inherits from the parent, including nested typography. `data-size` and `data-align` remain available without driving variant selectors.

Button variants configure private color values consumed by shared hover/active rules. Existing public button tokens remain the customization API. Native disabled state (including disabled fieldsets), `aria-disabled`, flat/raised behavior, focus, reduced motion and forced colors remain separate interaction concerns. Private `--_dui-*` variables are implementation details.

Ordinary children use the default padded content with its existing border/theme tokens. Supply a `content` snippet to replace that presentation with consumer-owned markup and scoped CSS; when supplied, it takes precedence over children. Absolute mode keeps a library-owned positioning, border and overflow frame around either presentation. The existing `caret(open)` snippet lets consumers own decorative caret markup and sizing.

```svelte
{#snippet content()}
{/snippet}
```

```svelte
<Details summary="Filters" position="absolute" align="end">
	<form><!-- native controls --></form>
</Details>
```

Screen-reader text renders only when a nonempty `text` is supplied; there is no default message. Supply translated text for standalone status spinners. For decorative use alongside an existing message, omit `text` and set `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden="true"` (or hide its wrapper). Native div attributes and callbacks pass through. Customize `--dui-loading-spinner-size`, `--dui-loading-spinner-color`, and `--dui-loading-spinner-border-width`; defaults retain the 80px current-color ripple. Supply an optional `feedback` snippet to replace the default StatusMessage inside the centering layout. Provide either `text` for the default or `feedback` for custom markup; the snippet takes precedence if both are supplied. Custom feedback owns its status/alert announcements, so the layout adds no extra live region.

```svelte
<LoadingScreen>
	{#snippet feedback()}
		<StatusMessage variant="error" text={failureMessage} />
		<Button onclick={retry}>{retryLabel}</Button>
	{/snippet}
</LoadingScreen>
```
Center a single translated startup message horizontally and vertically within a full viewport. Keep the page's main landmark in the caller.

```svelte
<main>
	<LoadingScreen text={loadingMessage} />
</main>
```

Use `variant="error"` for a failed startup without a spinner. The message uses StatusMessage's status/alert semantics; the spinner is decorative. Native div attributes, class and style are forwarded. Set `--dui-loading-screen-min-height` for a contained area; content grows naturally for long text and small viewports. Width and internal padding have corresponding `--dui-loading-screen-*` tokens. It does not add a main landmark, focus trap, autofocus, overlay or state management.

	<InputText label={draftLabel} bind:value={draft} />
	<Button type="button" onclick={save}>{saveLabel}</Button>
</LoadingContent>

Keeps child content mounted while `loading` is true (the default), preserving input state and
content layout. Pending content is dimmed, inert, and hidden from the accessibility tree; the
wrapper exposes `aria-busy`. A LoadingScreen shares a grid area with the retained content. When `loading` becomes false, the overlay is removed and the same controls become
usable. Focus is not moved or restored automatically; the caller owns focus when starting work
from inside the region. The region accommodates both retained content and feedback, so reserve sufficient space for
longer loading messages when needed.

Supply translated `text` and optionally `variant="error"`. The component does not fetch data,
interpret query state, retry, or provide fallback strings. Avoid adding a live role to the wrapper:
the overlay already supplies a status (or alert for errors). Without children, it renders a
standalone LoadingScreen regardless of `loading`, preserving the startup/error composition.
Native div attributes, callbacks, class, and style pass to the retained-content wrapper or the
standalone screen. LoadingScreen CSS properties customize the standalone presentation.

The snippet replaces the visible text while StatusMessage keeps its live-region root and decorative indicator; do not add another live region inside the snippet. Errors use `role="alert"` and the shared error color; other variants use `role="status"`. The spinner is excluded from the accessibility tree, leaving one live region. Native div attributes and callbacks, class, and style pass through. Override `role` or `aria-live` when the application supplies announcement behavior; avoid nesting inside another live region. For announcements of updates, keep the component mounted and update its text/variant rather than relying on initially rendered status text being announced.

The application owns visibility, loading/save state, translations, retry actions, and error mapping. The component accepts plain text and adds no dismissal, timer, form logic, or generic fallback messages. Spacing uses `gap`, and long text wraps. Children supply visually hidden supplementary text. Native span attributes pass through, including `id` for accessible description references. Keep interactive controls outside this component.

A reusable action drawer beneath caller-owned content. Swiping right reveals
`leftActions`; swiping left reveals `rightActions`. Sides describe the physical
location of the drawer, including in RTL layouts. Order actions from the first
stage to the final stage, with unique IDs within each side. Each action accepts
`id`, `label`, optional `disabled` and `dismissOnSwipe`, and the existing Button `variant` values.

A short horizontal drag reveals native action buttons when released. Dragging
35% of the row width arms the first enabled action; intermediate enabled actions
are spaced evenly up to the final action at 90%. With one enabled action, it is
reserved for the 90% full swipe. Releasing an armed swipe chooses that action;
moving back reduces or cancels the armed stage. Reopening a drawer requires a
deliberate additional drag before arming. Action labels keep the same wrapping
and text styling as their backgrounds expand. Once an action is armed, the other
actions fade to dimmed while it stays at full brightness. Retreating below the threshold
restores them; the cue also stays visible during a committed exit. Selection
changes only opacity, so label positions and wrapping remain unchanged.
A gesture never chooses an action until release. Disabled actions remain visible as disabled buttons and are skipped by
the progressive swipe stages.

Set `dismissOnSwipe: true` on the final enabled action to finish a full swipe off
the row instead of returning it to the closed position. On release, the final
action's background expands across the row and covers the other buttons while
the content slides away. Its label retains its width and text styling. It works independently
of `variant`: archive can dismiss without destructive styling, while trash can
use both. Releasing at the 90% threshold commits the exit; retreating or
cancelling before release still backs out. The row becomes inert during the exit
and hidden when it finishes. `onactionchosen` fires once after the native CSS
exit and fill transitions complete, so the app can remove its list item without interrupting
the animation. With reduced motion or zero duration, completion is immediate.
Choosing a button or an earlier action retains the ordinary callback behavior.

To restore a retained row after an undo or failed operation, bind the component
instance (`bind:this={swipeRow}`) and call `swipeRow.reset()`. Resetting during an
exit cancels its pending notification. The component does not delete data or
remove the consuming app's `li`.

`onactionchosen` is a typed Svelte 5 callback receiving `{ id, side, source }`,
where `side` is `left` or `right` and `source` is `swipe` or `button`. The component
closes after an ordinary choice, or exits for an opted-in final full swipe. The consuming app owns archiving, deleting, confirmations,
async work, persistence, and item removal. The callback does not receive a
CustomEvent or `.detail`. The package also exports the `SwipeAction`,
`SwipeActionChosen`, and `SwipeSide` types.

Native Pointer Events handle touch, mouse and pen; CSS `touch-action: pan-y
pinch-zoom` preserves vertical scrolling and pinch zoom. Gesture tracking locks
only after horizontal intent. Cancellation, lost capture, window blur, resizing,
and action/disabled changes back out without choosing. Ordinary taps and keyboard
link activation retain their native behavior; a completed horizontal drag
suppresses the resulting click. Starts on buttons, inputs, selects, textareas,
summaries, editable content, or descendants marked `data-swipe-ignore` do not start
a swipe. Browser/OS edge-navigation gestures remain browser-owned.

Actions stay underneath the row in the same fixed-height container. The row
slides aside to expose solid, edge-to-edge action surfaces; it has no visible
menu trigger or separate expanded panel. `actionsLabel` supplies the group's
accessible name. For keyboard access, focus the row link and press ArrowRight to
reveal the left drawer or ArrowLeft to reveal the right drawer. These keys slide
the same row and focus its first enabled action. Escape closes it and returns
focus to the row. For content without a focusable child, give SwipeActions
`tabindex={0}`. Native action buttons stay inert and hidden from the accessibility
tree until their side is revealed. `disabled` cancels the interaction while
leaving caller-owned content available.

The root is a `div`: place it inside the consuming app's `li` when building a
list. Supply the row's anchor/content as children; do not wrap SwipeActions in a
link or another list item inside it. Native root attributes,
class and style pass through. Customize `--dui-swipe-background-color` (defaults to
the theme background), `--dui-swipe-action-width` (5.5rem) and
`--dui-swipe-duration` (180ms). Button variants and focus styles use the existing
theme; corners remain square, and reduced-motion preferences disable settling
and dimming animations. XState is the only added runtime dependency; there is no gesture
library or Svelte adapter dependency.

Interaction ownership is a private XState machine: closed/open rest,
pointer tracking, yielding to vertical scrolling, revealing/armed drag, and a
single chosen-action emission. The Svelte wrapper owns native event listeners,
pointer capture, measurement, focus, and actor teardown. Storybook includes both
directions, three progressive actions, full-swipe dismissal with reset, one-sided actions, disabled actions,
disabling, and a scrollable mobile list.

The header is black with white text; `data-dui-theme="dark"` reverses it to white with black text. Thin lines separate body rows and underline the header. Use `closeControl(close, label)` to replace the default close button. Render an accessibly named native control and invoke the supplied callback; `label` is the translated `closeLabel`. Drawer retains panel visibility, scoped Escape and focus restoration. `showCloseButton={false}` hides the custom control too. 	{#snippet closeControl(close, label)}

It defaults to `0`, preserving the borderless panel. Set it through the Drawer’s native `style` attribute or an inherited custom property; consumers do not need to select the internal panel element.

`mode` defaults to `overlay`, composing native Dialog into a full-height side panel. Required `heading` and `closeLabel` are caller-owned; heading also accepts a snippet. `side` defaults to `left`, with `right` available. Optional `bind:open` controls visibility. The compact × close button uses the required translated closeLabel as its accessible name. Set `headingHidden` to keep the heading available to screen readers without showing it. The close button and Escape dismiss it. Overlay mode keeps keyboard focus inside, makes the background inert and restores focus through native dialog behavior. `closedby` defaults to `any` for browser-supported outside-click dismissal.

Set `mode="inline"` for a collapsible sidebar in normal page layout. It renders a labelled `aside`, with no dialog/modal role, backdrop, background inertness or focus trap. Put it beside the page content in a flex/grid container to reserve actual layout space. Keep DOM order consistent with visual order: place a right sidebar after the content rather than reordering it with CSS. The application chooses responsive breakpoints; the stories stack content on narrow screens.

For inline mode, give the toggle `aria-controls` referencing the drawer's `id` and `aria-expanded={menuOpen}`. Opening leaves focus on the toggle. Closing while focus is inside restores focus before hiding the panel; optional `triggerId` identifies a persistent return target, including initially open or programmatically opened sidebars. Otherwise the element focused when opening is used. Escape dismisses inline mode only when focus is inside. Outside clicks do not close it. Closed content is hidden and inert immediately, including during exit animation. Changing modes closes the drawer to avoid carrying focus across incompatible interaction contexts.

Native attributes/events, class and style pass through to the active container; dialog-only `closedby` applies only in overlay mode. Triggers, Navigation and link/route-selection behavior remain caller-owned. For an inline sidebar, links need not collapse it. Use gap for sibling layout spacing; internal panel padding uses Dialog tokens.

Overlay mode slides/fades; inline mode animates its reserved width. Both respect reduced motion, and retain the inert visual panel until exit motion finishes. Inline focus restoration waits for caller-hidden triggers to become visible. Without motion support, visibility changes immediately. Both variants fill the viewport height by default; inline placement sticks to the top during page scrolling. The body scrolls independently beneath the close control. Set `--dui-drawer-height` for a contained layout. Customize `--dui-drawer-width` (default `24rem`), `--dui-drawer-gap` and `--dui-drawer-duration` (default `200ms`). Colors, borders and padding use Dialog tokens; backdrop tokens apply only to overlay mode. No touch/swipe gesture or automatic responsive breakpoint is included.
See the [accessibility specification](docs/finance-component-spec.md#drawer--implemented-awaiting-review) for each mode's behavior and pending verification.
